tree_branches.name: Warragamba Dam
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Warragamba Dam
tree_branches.text: Mrs JUDY HANNAN ( Wollondilly ) ( 18:0 7 :19 ): Warragamba Dam was officially opened by former New South Wales Premier Bob Heffron on 14 October 1960—so this year is its birthday. The ceremony was attended by thousands of guests, workers and their families for a day of celebration. The opening included an opening of the dam's crest gates, releasing a spectacular display of water. Warragamba Dam was built to address Sydney's critical water shortage during World War II and was never intended to be a flood mitigation dam. Work began in 1948. Warragamba Dam is the largest domestic water supply dam in the world. It holds over 2,000 gigalitres of water for Sydney's supply. Approximately 1,800 men of more than 25 nationalities worked on building the dam. Many of those workers were post-World War II immigrants who came to Australia for a new life and lived in the temporary town of Warragamba during the construction period—a town that still survives today. Fifteen people died during the construction of the dam and its associated emergency supply scheme from workplace accidents including falling objects and equipment malfunctions.

tree_branches.name: Mrs JUDY HANNAN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Warragamba Dam > Mrs JUDY HANNAN
tree_branches.text: Mrs JUDY HANNAN ( Wollondilly ) —It is with respect that I honour the life and legacy of Mrs. Marion Palmer of Bargo. Marion, born 1st May 1943, was a woman of grace, strength, and unwavering devotion to her family and her passing on 10th July 2025 was felt by all who knew her. She was the beloved wife of William, whose partnership she cherished throughout their years together. Marion was a devoted mother to Peter, Robyne, and David, and a supportive mother-in-law to Dave. Her nurturing spirit and steadfast love were the foundation of her family. Marion's memory lives on through her grandchildren—Kara, Grant, Luke, Ryan, and Aaron—each of whom she adored deeply. Her joy was further multiplied by her great-grandchildren: Charlotte, Liam, Atticus, Pixiella, Harriet, Hamish, Finn, and Hudson, who brought her immense pride and happiness. Her presence enriched the lives of all who knew her. Marion will be remembered for her kindness, wisdom, and enduring love.

tree_branches.name: Newcastle Jets
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Newcastle Jets
tree_branches.text: Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP ( Newcastle ) ( 18:0 8 :28 ): Saturday 4 October marked a momentous day for Newcastle, with the Jets winning the 2025 Australia Cup against Victoria's Heidelberg United. It was a real nailbiter, with Heidelberg scoring in the first 10 minutes, but by half-time the Jets had equalised, with Burgess finding the back of the net. A tense second half saw many goals denied, ending 90 minutes at one-all and taking the teams into extra time. The Jets needed something huge to break the deadlock, and Oscar Fryer delivered, with a powerful shot from the edge of the penalty box. It gave the team the energy for Ben Gibson to score the third and final goal with five minutes left. The Australia Cup is the Jets' first piece of silverware in almost 20 years, but I have a feeling this young team are taking the Jets to the top in the upcoming A-League season, with their first game this Sunday. Go the Jets!

tree_branches.name: Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Newcastle Jets > Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP
tree_branches.text: Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP ( Newcastle ) —I want to congratulate Phoenix Denny on his recent competition in the 2025 World Scholars Global Round in Thailand. Pheonix is a year 6 student at St Joseph's Primary School Merewether. He is the first High Potential and Gifted Education student to represent the Maitland‑Newcastle Catholic Diocese at an international competition. The World Scholars Cup was established as an alternative to traditional academic competitions, with small teams competing in challenges, multiple choice tests, debate and collaborative writing. Phoenix's passion and skill for debating saw him shine at the regional round and allowing him to advance to the global round. I want to congratulate Phoenix on his incredible efforts, and look forward to seeing what he accomplishes in the future.

tree_branches.name: Anthony "Harries" Carroll
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Anthony "Harries" Carroll
tree_branches.text: Ms KELLIE SLOANE ( Vaucluse ) ( 18:0 9 :23 ): I congratulate Anthony "Harries" Carroll on the launch of his new book Harries : The L ifeguard from Bondi Beach . Harries is well known in our community, looking after us for over 30 years as a lifeguard on Bondi Beach. In that role, Harries has been a friendly face, rescuing thousands of people. But Harries was not always confident. He was bullied as a child for dyslexia. His life changed when he discovered he could see and hear things that others could not. With his heightened alertness, Harries says he can anticipate when someone might be in danger, which has served him well as a lifeguard. Harries' book is a hopeful story about how we sometimes need to dig a little deeper to find our special gifts. Speaking of that gift, I also acknowledge his recent rescue while on holiday in Hawaii where he resuscitated a three-year-old boy who had been lying in the surf, saving his life. Harries is a true hero, and we appreciate what he does at home and abroad.

tree_branches.name: Ms KELLIE SLOANE
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Anthony "Harries" Carroll > Ms KELLIE SLOANE
tree_branches.text: Ms KELLIE SLOANE ( Vaucluse ) —I would like to congratulate Double Bay Sailing Club on their successful Double Bay Regatta held on Saturday 11th October, 2025. This was the inaugural regatta and was open to all ILCA / Laser sailors from Sydney and beyond, with three races held on the single day in Sydney Harbour. The winning sailor from each class had their name inscribed on the Mark Bathwaite Trophy, named after the Double Bay Sailing Club legend. Congratulations to DBSC on a successful event and looking forward to many more in the years to come!

tree_branches.name: Peter Lawley
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Peter Lawley
tree_branches.text: Ms LIESL TESCH ( Gosford ) ( 18:1 0 :29 ): I acknowledge the valuable work of Peter Lawley as he retires from the Gosford Erina Business Chamber and from his leading role with Legacy. The chamber has been a staple of the business and commerce community on the Central Coast and has been important in growing local business in the region. Peter has been a board member of Gosford Erina Business Chamber since 2020 and president since 2022. Peter has been the CEO of Brisbane Water Legacy since 2010 and has also been involved with the organisation on a national level, serving as national aged care coordinator, on the advocacy committee between 2012 and 2021, as acting chief executive of Legacy Australia in 2018, as a delegate in the National Aged Care Alliance, and as a delegate on the Department of Veterans' Affairs' National Aged and Community Care Forum between 2013 and 2021. His tireless work earned him an Order of Australia medal in the 2023 King's Birthday Honours for service to veterans and their families. Peter is a lifelong Coastie who grew up in Gosford and has been passionate about giving something back to the community that nurtured him, as well as helping the business sector across the region. I thank him for his tireless work in our community.

tree_branches.name: Ms LIESL TESCH
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Peter Lawley > Ms LIESL TESCH
tree_branches.text: Ms LIESL TESCH ( Gosford ) ( 19:40 :36 ): I congratulate the member for Newcastle on his advocacy for the live music scene. In opposition, he was banging the drum for live music in his community. I also congratulate all of the artists involved. With 54 million views, I am definitely going to look that one up. I also acknowledge the venues and the precincts. It is a lot of work to pull all this together. It is important for the night‑time economy and the young people of our communities to have a place to be. On that note, I also thank our Minister for Music and the Night-time Economy and our 24-Hour Economy Commission. Labor has made a huge commitment to the night-time economy and the live music scene across New South Wales. In closing, Labor loves live music.

tree_branches.name: Ryde Electorate Netball Umpires
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Ryde Electorate Netball Umpires
tree_branches.text: Mr JORDAN LANE ( Ryde ) ( 18:1 1 :34 ): I ask the House to join me in congratulating some of the amazing umpires in my electorate who were recently recognised by the Eastwood Ryde Netball Association [ERNA] for the contribution they have made to the sport. They are Jacquelyn Osborne, Riley Chantler, Sophie Vaughan, Patrick O'Malveney, Natalie Jukic and Phoebe Wheatley. The umpires give their time, energy and expertise to ensure our games are played fairly and in the true spirit of competition. From junior matches at Brush Farm to senior fixtures at Meadowbank, the volunteers uphold the integrity of the game and model the respect and discipline that netball is built upon. They are mentors for aspiring umpires, leaders on the court and champions of community sport. Whether in rain or shine, early mornings or long afternoons, they show up, not for accolades but for love of the game and their local community. I thank all ERNA umpires past and present. Our community is better for their service, and netball in Ryde continues to thrive because of them.

tree_branches.name: Mr JORDAN LANE
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Ryde Electorate Netball Umpires > Mr JORDAN LANE
tree_branches.text: Mr JORDAN LANE ( Ryde ) —I rise today to ask the House to join me in recognising and congratulating Melrose Estate Agents for winning the 2025 Northern District Local Business Award in the Outstanding Real Estate Agency category. This being the 3rd win for this business, this is an extraordinary achievement and a well deserved one indeed. Melrose Estate Agents has redefined what it means to be a real estate agency, placing clients and their goals at the heart of everything they do. More than simply facilitating property transactions, they have combined expert knowledge, genuine care, and a fresh, client-first perspective, helping individuals not only navigate the property market but also realise their broader aspirations. Their approach is grounded in building long-lasting relationships and delivering real value at every step. Melrose's success reflects the strength and evolution of Ryde's business community - one that values innovation, trust, and putting people first. Your passion and perseverance have not gone unnoticed.

tree_branches.name: Saim Saeed
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Saim Saeed
tree_branches.text: Ms KYLIE WILKINSON ( East Hills ) ( 18:1 2 :33 ): I recognise local young shining star East Hills Boys High School student Saim Saeed for his academic excellence, community service and political advocacy. Saim recently participated in the New South Wales Youth Parliament program, where he was selected by his peers as the youth shadow Minister for Education. His committee introduced a bill to ensure equitable access to alternative education pathways in New South Wales, which was passed during youth sitting week. For his outstanding contributions, Saim received the Joel Mackay Youth Voice Award, recognising his outstanding advocacy and commitment to community engagement. Saim also delivered a community recognition statement about the impact of the Gaza conflict, which was a thoughtful and compassionate reflection on justice and solidarity. Closer to home, Saim has shown the same drive by lobbying for improvements to his school's facilities and being elected president of the Condell Park Australian Labor Party branch. With early acceptance into the University of New South Wales, his future is bright. Congratulations, Saim.

tree_branches.name: Ms KYLIE WILKINSON
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Saim Saeed > Ms KYLIE WILKINSON
tree_branches.text: Ms KYLIE WILKINSON ( East Hills ) —Congratulations to the Bankstown Bruins coaches and managers who have been recognised with awards this year. Special recognition goes to Cooper Avery for receiving the Coaching Recognition Award, to Spiro Stamatatos and Lauryn Curtin for being named Robbie Cadee Coaches of the Year, and to Kate Filemu for her excellent work as manager. These honours reflect your outstanding leadership, commitment, and the vital role you play in the success of the team. I also want to congratulate the Bankstown Bruins on an impressive season. Your dedication, teamwork, and perseverance have truly paid off, and it's inspiring to see local talent performing at such a high level on the basketball court. The Bruins are an important part of our East Hills community. By bringing people together from all backgrounds, you've built a strong sense of unity and pride that extends beyond the game. Thank you to the players, coaches, volunteers, and supporters who have made this success possible. I look forward to seeing the Bruins continue to grow and inspire future generations. Congratulations again!

tree_branches.name: Willoughby Electorate Higher School Certificate Students
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Willoughby Electorate Higher School Certificate Students
tree_branches.text: Mr TIM JAMES ( Willoughby ) ( 18:1 3 :41 ): I congratulate the class of 2025 as they complete high school and sit their final HSC exams. That is a proud milestone that reflects years of hard work, commitment and perseverance. I acknowledge all year 12 students across the high schools of the Willoughby electorate: Bradfield Senior College, Cammeraygal High School, Chatswood High School, Glenaeon Rudolf Steiner School, Mercy Catholic College, Naremburn School, Redlands, St Pius X College and Willoughby Girls High School. Well done to every student on reaching an important point in their educational journey. I thank the teachers whose professionalism, guidance and encouragement have shaped and supported students and helped them reach their potential. Their commitment leaves a lasting impact. I extend my gratitude to parents and families for the love and support they have given their children through that chapter. I congratulate the class of 2025 on all they have achieved so far. I wish them every success and good luck in their final exams and the exciting opportunities that lie ahead.

tree_branches.name: Mr TIM JAMES
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Willoughby Electorate Higher School Certificate Students > Mr TIM JAMES
tree_branches.text: Mr TIM JAMES ( Willoughby ) —Ms Unity Taylor-Hill has made an outstanding contribution to public education through a decade of leadership at Anzac Park Public School in Cammeray. As the school's inaugural principal, appointed when Anzac Park PS was established in 2015, she has shaped its vision, culture and identity from day one. Under her leadership, Anzac Park has grown into a thriving, innovative and highly regarded public school, known for its strong community spirit, modern approach to learning and commitment to student success. Ms Taylor-Hill guided the school through its formative years, overseeing enrolment growth, developing contemporary teaching practices, and fostering an inclusive and collaborative school community. After ten years of dedicated service, Ms Taylor-Hill has now been promoted to the role of Leader – Primary Curriculum within the NSW Department of Education. This is a well-deserved recognition of her expertise and leadership. The Anzac Park Public School community deeply thanks Ms Taylor-Hill for her years of service and wishes her every success in this important new role supporting schools across the state.

tree_branches.name: Burwood and Auburn Police Area Commands
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Burwood and Auburn Police Area Commands
tree_branches.text: Mr JASON LI ( Strathfield ) ( 18:1 4 :35 ): I acknowledge the outstanding and brave work of officers from the Burwood Police Area Command and Auburn Police Area Command, led by Superintendent Christine McDonald and Superintendent Robert Toynton respectively, who responded to two serious incidents in our community last week. On 5 October, officers from Burwood Police Area Command led a major operation in Croydon Park after a public-place shooting. With support from specialist units, they entered a dangerous situation, arrested a man and restored safety to the area. Their courage and professionalism protected lives. In Strathfield, another distressing incident left many in our community shaken. I extend my thoughts to the victim, her family and the child who had to witness such trauma. Officers from Auburn Police Area Command acted swiftly and compassionately, arresting the alleged offender. I thank all the officers and first responders involved. Their bravery, care and commitment keep our community safe. Strathfield remains one of the safest and most inclusive places in Australia, and we each share a responsibility to keep it that way.

tree_branches.name: Issy Weaven
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Issy Weaven
tree_branches.text: Mr JUSTIN CLANCY ( Albury ) ( 18:1 5 :44 ): I acknowledge the outstanding achievement of Issy Weaven, a dedicated student who has successfully combined her senior studies with a traineeship in health services at Holbrook hospital. Issy was given an incredible opportunity through Murrumbidgee Local Health District to embark on the traineeship when she commenced year 11. Over the past two years, she has completed more than 800 hours of practical training in the Harry Jarvis Wing, working alongside highly skilled nurses to provide patient care, from showering and dressing to monitoring blood pressure and offering daily support. Alongside her hands‑on training, Issy also undertook weekly online TAFE studies. Through the experience, Issy discovered a genuine passion for helping people and developed the skills and confidence to pursue her dream career in nursing. With the successful completion of both her TAFE studies and practical hours, Issy has now proudly attained her certificate III in health services, qualifying her to begin working in a hospital setting straight away. I thank Holbrook hospital, TAFE and her school for providing the opportunity for our students. Issy has created an exciting pathway for her future in nursing.

tree_branches.name: Mr JUSTIN CLANCY
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Issy Weaven > Mr JUSTIN CLANCY
tree_branches.text: Mr JUSTIN CLANCY ( Albury ) —I acknowledge Charles Sturt University as it celebrates 20 years of delivering nursing education at the Albury campus, a milestone that reflects dedication to strengthening our regional healthcare workforce. Since its first intake in 2005, the Bachelor of Nursing program has trained approximately 700 nurses locally, giving aspiring healthcare professionals in the twin cities the opportunity to study and serve close to home. Today, Charles Sturt University stands as the largest provider of registered nursing education in regional Australia, a remarkable achievement. Between 2020 and 2024, an estimated 2,000 students have graduated from the Bachelor of Nursing program, an average of 500 nursing graduates each year. This year alone, over 3,150 students are studying a Bachelor of Nursing through Charles Sturt, with 153 based in Albury-Wodonga. I thank Professor Kerryn Butler-Henderson, Head of Nursing, Paramedicine and Healthcare Sciences, and to the entire teaching and support team, for their role in this success. With 93% of undergraduate and 97 per cent of postgraduate nursing graduates securing full-time employment within four months, Charles Sturt University leads the nation in nursing graduate employability. Congratulations on 20 years of service to our region and beyond!

tree_branches.name: Imad Gendy
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Imad Gendy
tree_branches.text: Ms CHARISHMA KALIYANDA ( Liverpool ) ( 18:1 6 :50 ): According to a Japanese proverb, better than a thousand days of diligent study is one day with a great teacher. Imagine the many thousands of days of study that Imad Gendy has saved for his students. Mr Gendy recently reached the incredible milestone of 30 years of dedicated service to public education. He is a much-loved mathematics teacher at James Busby High School, where he has inspired generations of students through his passion for learning and commitment to their success. Over three decades, Mr Gendy has not only taught mathematics but also instilled confidence, curiosity and resilience in his students. James Busby is one of those schools where many of the current teachers are former students. Teachers like Mr Gendy embody the best of our public education system. Their patience, care and consistency create lasting impacts on the lives of young people across the Green Valley area. His colleagues and students alike speak of his kindness, professionalism and genuine desire to see every student reach their potential. I congratulate Mr Gendy on the remarkable achievement and thank him for his lifelong contribution to education and our community.

tree_branches.name: Ms CHARISHMA KALIYANDA
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Imad Gendy > Ms CHARISHMA KALIYANDA
tree_branches.text: Ms CHARISHMA KALIYANDA ( Liverpool ) ( 20:14 :15 ): I respond to highlight the serious and concerning issues raised by the member for Leppington in his statement. We share the Liverpool local government area, and I know that many of my constituents and many of the residents of the Liverpool local government area have expressed deep dissatisfaction and disappointment with the shenanigans—if I may frame it that way—that are being reported widely in the media about what has taken place in the council, where residents' concerns are being deprioritised for politicking and lawfare. In this term of government, this Government has made a concerted effort to restore faith in democracy and in government institutions by prioritising accountability. I call on the Opposition to support any actions and any measures taken in this respect as well.

tree_branches.name: New South Wales Youth Parliament
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > New South Wales Youth Parliament
tree_branches.text: Mr ALISTER HENSKENS ( Wahroonga ) ( 18:1 7 :04 ): Recently I met two inspiring young men who took part in the New South Wales Youth Parliament. Harry Burwood of Knox Grammar School represented the Wahroonga electorate and Patrick McCarthy of Gosford High School represented the Gosford electorate, even though he lives in the Wahroonga electorate. Both men are intelligent and driven. They spoke fondly of their time at Youth Parliament learning how to make policies and draft legislation. Harry is part of the Youth Committee at the Sydney Jewish Museum, an event manager at Youth 4 Difference and a sergeant in the Australian Army Cadets. He also volunteers at different organisations across the community. Patrick was a prefect at Normanhurst West Public School and is part of the leadership program at Gosford High School. He is a regular volunteer at Thornleigh Community Baptist Church and Thornleigh Baseball where he is currently captain of the under-19s team. Both young men show genuine enthusiasm and passion for politics. Their deep sense of volunteering is a fantastic starting point for their future careers. I wish Patrick and Harry good luck with their future endeavours.

tree_branches.name: Mr ALISTER HENSKENS
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > New South Wales Youth Parliament > Mr ALISTER HENSKENS
tree_branches.text:
Mr ALISTER HENSKENS ( Wahroonga ) ( 18:27 :25 ): A highlight of each year for me is when I host two high school leaders from each secondary school in the Wahroonga electorate for a tour and special dinner in the President's Dining Room at Parliament House here in Macquarie Street. This annual tradition—commenced by my predecessor, as member for Ku-ring-gai—has now survived a redistribution and provides these remarkable young people with an opportunity to understand some of our State's democratic history, to witness its democratic processes in action and to better understand how decisions made in this place affect lives and communities. It also provides me with a valuable opportunity to hear directly from our young people about their perspectives on various issues.

Every year, without exception, I am deeply impressed by the confidence, curiosity and engagement of our young leaders. Their level of maturity and insight reflects the strong values instilled in them by their families, schools and teachers. The students in attendance this year were Jazarah Tambyrajah and Nell Owen from Abbotsleigh, Huntley Stace and Bea Meyer from Barker College, Ruby Young and Helen Bui from Hornsby Girls High School, Arjun Vishnu and Chester Swaffer from Knox Grammar School, Keenor Sabaa and Lucy McKenna from Loreto Normanhurst, Ashwyn Tyagi and Ashton Huynh from Normanhurst Boys High School, Abigail Chapman and Thomas Passe-de Silva from Pennant Hills High School, Ang-Ya Koo and Emily Abadee from Pymble Ladies' College, Maya Manjah and Eliza Waugh from St Leo's Catholic College, Sophie Robinson and Angus Lloyd from Turramurra High School, and Audrey Kennedy and Toby Pope from Wahroonga Adventist School. These young leaders are aspirational, intelligent and forward-thinking.

During our conversations, many shared their ambitions for the future, expressing a strong desire to contribute meaningfully to society. They spoke about pursuing varied careers in areas such as law, engineering, science and even actuarial studies, showing a passion about learning more about our world and building our future communities. A number of students also shared their interest in healthcare professions such as physiotherapy and medicine, motivated by a desire to help others and improve quality of life. It was clear that these students possess both ambition and compassion—qualities that will undoubtedly serve them and our State well in the future.

We also spoke about their broader hopes for the future, from attending university and studying abroad, to travelling and experiencing life beyond their local communities. Their eagerness to learn and to explore the world reminded me of the importance of nurturing curiosity and global awareness in our young people. When I finished high school, I too had the opportunity to travel, spending several months backpacking through Europe. It remains one of the most rewarding experiences of my life. I was able to visit family in the Netherlands, immerse myself in different cultures and see firsthand the diversity and richness of the world beyond Australia. That experience broadened my perspectives and deepened my appreciation for the opportunities we have here at home.

As these students approach such a significant milestone, I encouraged them to maintain a sense of balance and wellbeing. It is important that they do not become overwhelmed by pressure or lose sight of what brings them happiness. Making time for friends, family and the activities they enjoy is essential for making it through the end of school. Those moments of connection and rest are not distractions; they are what sustain us through the most challenging periods of our lives. This week, many year 12 students will commence their HSC exams—the culmination of 13 years of schooling, effort and dedication. I wish all the students across New South Wales who are sitting their HSC exams this year the very best and congratulate them on completing high school. The Wahroonga electorate is an educational powerhouse, with the most HSC students each year in our State. I had the opportunity to attend the graduation ceremonies of those high schools during the last week of term 3. Those ceremonies were an important time to celebrate all that the year 12 students had achieved and to recognise the high achievers of each school before they undertake their final exams.

Finally, I remind students that while academic results are important, they do not define a person's worth or future potential. Success takes many forms, and often life provides unexpected opportunities. Even if the first pathway does not unfold exactly as they had planned, they will have countless ways to reach their goals. With determination, curiosity and persistence, they can achieve whatever they set their mind to. I genuinely believe that success is 10 per cent inspiration and 90 per cent perspiration. I encourage every student to stick out whatever they wish to do. Go well, and congratulations on completing high school.

tree_branches.name: Southern Life Church
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Southern Life Church
tree_branches.text: Dr MICHAEL HOLLAND ( Bega ) ( 18: 18 :04 ): I rise to congratulate the Southern Life Church, Moruya, and the South Coast Health and Sustainability Alliance [SHASA]. With the assistance of a New South Wales Government infrastructure grant of over $168,000, Southern Life Church and SHASA undertook works to enable the church food hall and church hall to operate as havens during extreme weather events. Works included solar panels and batteries, electrical upgrades to the switchboard for both buildings, installation of satellite communications, two rainwater tanks, a fire pump, hoses and fittings to enable fighting ember attacks, four internal air filters to address wood smoke, a back-up 30kVA diesel generator for the food hall and weatherproof enclosures for the electrical equipment. Southern Life Church has funded a generator for the church hall, an additional rainwater tank, and concrete slabs for the rainwater tanks and generators. Catering for up to 200 people, the Southern Life Church haven will be a refuge for vulnerable members of the Moruya community during extreme events like bushfires and heatwaves.

Dr MICHAEL HOLLAND ( Bega ) ( 18:22 :43 ): On Monday 15 September, I was pleased to attend the sod turning event for the new Moruya High School support unit. Construction has begun on the new $7 million support unit, while another $13 million in upgrades is on the way for the school as part of the Minns Labor Government's work to rebuild public education and ensure students in regional New South Wales have access to every opportunity to achieve their full potential. The new support unit will contain seven permanent support classrooms with practical activities areas, breakout spaces, an outdoor play area, a covered outdoor learning area, accessible toilets and change rooms, laundry, kitchen, staff room and a new access road with undercover drop-off area and car-parking facilities. The project is due for completion by term 2, 2026, replacing five ageing demountables which were a legacy of the former Liberal-Nationals Government.

The new support unit will better support students with disabilities, ensuring all students have access to the same educational opportunities. This will provide students with the safe and supportive environment they deserve. This support unit will not only enhance learning but also ensure that families in Moruya and across the region know their children are being given the best chance to thrive. Moruya High School is also one of the 33 schools across New South Wales to receive a share of a $100 million investment from the New South Wales Government as part of the High Potential and Gifted Education [HPGE] partner schools program.

Moruya High School will receive facility upgrades to accommodate increased enrolments, broaden educational opportunities and facilitate the delivery of tailored HPGE course offerings. These opportunities include activities such as class-level acceleration programs, inter-school competitions and tournaments, and other statewide opportunities. The works will include upgrades to science, technology, engineering and mathematics classrooms, technology and applied studies classrooms, and the music room, performance area and sound studio. Works will also include upgrading the sports court, which will include a new court surface, fencing and line marking; updating the science lab, library and administration buildings; installing air conditioning across the school; improving senior lockers; a new covered walkway; and an automated front gate.

Staff at these schools will work with HPGE experts to deliver more opportunities that challenge and extend students to reach their potential. Teachers will receive dedicated professional learning to assist with identifying and rolling out more High Potential and Gifted Education opportunities for their students. Broader professional learning will also be provided to teachers in all New South Wales public schools as part of the Minns Labor Government's commitment to expanding access to High Potential and Gifted Education opportunities across the system.

Families in the Eurobodalla can also look forward to improved public schools under the Minns Labor Government, including High Potential and Gifted Education upgrades at Batemans Bay High School as well as a new school hall for Mogo Public School. The Batemans Bay High School development includes upgrades to the food technology and vocational education and training kitchen; to five science laboratories, including three prep rooms; and to two woodwork rooms, two metal work rooms and storage space. These works are part of the Minns Labor Government's plan to rebuild public education with a record $2.1 billion in the 2025-26 budget for new and upgraded schools across regional New South Wales.

A new hall and learning space will be constructed at Mogo Public School thanks to the latest round of funding under the Albanese Federal Government's schools upgrade fund. Mogo Public School has been granted $1.7 million under round two of the fund, which aims to assist public schools with the greatest need, including schools with high numbers of students from low-socio economic backgrounds, First Nations students and students with disability. The Minns Labor Government is making sure that time spent in the classroom is well spent. Under the previous Liberal Government, teachers were leaving the profession in droves resulting in 10,000 merged or cancelled classes each day. Under a Minns Labor Government, teacher vacancy rates have dropped.

Since coming to government, we have reduced the number of vacancies by 76 per cent in the Bega electorate. That means that our kids are spending more time learning in class and receiving more attention from their teachers. Our students have regained approximately half a million hours of lost learning as a result. In contrast to the former Liberal-Nationals Government, the Minns Labor Government is making teachers permanent. We are investing in public education, making over 16,000 temporary teachers and support staff permanent and increasing teachers' pay to attract and retain our best and brightest. This is part of a record investment in school infrastructure under the 2025-26 New South Wales budget, ensuring every student, regardless of postcode, can reach their full potential.

tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Community Recognition Statements > Prego Charcoal Chicken > Mr JORDAN LANE
tree_branches.text: Mr JORDAN LANE ( Ryde ) —I rise today to ask the House to join me in recognising and congratulating Melrose Estate Agents for winning the 2025 Northern District Local Business Award in the Outstanding Real Estate Agency category. This being the 3rd win for this business, this is an extraordinary achievement and a well deserved one indeed. Melrose Estate Agents has redefined what it means to be a real estate agency, placing clients and their goals at the heart of everything they do. More than simply facilitating property transactions, they have combined expert knowledge, genuine care, and a fresh, client-first perspective, helping individuals not only navigate the property market but also realise their broader aspirations. Their approach is grounded in building long-lasting relationships and delivering real value at every step. Melrose's success reflects the strength and evolution of Ryde's business community - one that values innovation, trust, and putting people first. Your passion and perseverance have not gone unnoticed.

The Wahroonga electorate is an educational powerhouse, with the most HSC students each year in our State. I had the opportunity to attend the graduation ceremonies of those high schools during the last week of term 3. Those ceremonies were an important time to celebrate all that the year 12 students had achieved and to recognise the high achievers of each school before they undertake their final exams.

Finally, I remind students that while academic results are important, they do not define a person's worth or future potential. Success takes many forms, and often life provides unexpected opportunities. Even if the first pathway does not unfold exactly as they had planned, they will have countless ways to reach their goals. With determination, curiosity and persistence, they can achieve whatever they set their mind to. I genuinely believe that success is 10 per cent inspiration and 90 per cent perspiration. I encourage every student to stick out whatever they wish to do. Go well, and congratulations on completing high school.

tree_branches.name: Government Performance
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Private Members' Statements > Government Performance
tree_branches.text:
It took a Labor government to finally deliver an accessibility upgrade of Macquarie Fields station, to build a long-awaited high school for the many families of Edmondson Park, to confront the housing challenge in New South Wales, to rebuild essential services, to invest in new local preschools, to provide more support classes and to give teachers and other frontline workers a well-deserved pay rise. Since its election in March 2023, the Labor Government has also been keen to help families with the cost of living. It introduced a $60 weekly toll cap for motorists, particularly those from areas like south-west Sydney, like my local community of Macquarie Fields, and other parts of Western Sydney, where people are forced to take the toll roads to get to and from work or to see their friends. Those long commutes are not only slow and painful but also financially prohibitive. That is why the $60 weekly toll cap has been so important.

The list does not end there. The Minns Labor Government has introduced historic rental reforms. We ushered in a new era of stability and security for the State's 2.3 million renters. As housing affordability continues to be a challenge, more and more people will rent, and they will be renting for longer. A typical renter now is not just a young Australian, fresh out of university, trying to share a house with some friends; renters are represented across all household types and sizes. That is why our rental reforms are important, modernising rental laws for the needs of our modern community. Such reforms include ending no-ground evictions, making it easier to have pets in rentals, limiting rent increases to once per year and banning fees for background checks.

The Government is getting on with the job of delivering for the people of New South Wales, particularly in my local area. I am thrilled to see work progressing at Macquarie Fields station. The project includes the installation of two new lifts and a new passenger footbridge. They will create an improved experience for our elderly, those with disability, and carers and parents with prams or carrying lots of shopping. The station will be modernised with a new accessible entry forecourt, improved canopy coverage, accessible parking and landscaping. The project is on track for delivery. The Macquarie Fields station upgrade is a wonderful example of a long and hard-fought community campaign. It is a major win for our local area and comes after years of advocacy. I thank my local community for their perseverance and patience over so many years and now, during this construction phase.

It took this Labor Government to restore fairness and integrity to station upgrades. We clearly recollect how the former Liberal Government shamelessly pork-barrelled station upgrades, making a mockery of the Transport Access Program. In 2020 the Auditor-General slammed the former Liberal Government for politicising station upgrades. It should not matter who the local member is; it should only matter what the needs of the community are. Our rapidly growing communities have long been crying out for new infrastructure. Local families have long been calling for a high school in Edmondson Park, and I am pleased to say that progress is well underway. The new high school will include fit-for-purpose classrooms and core facilities to meet enrolment demand in Edmondson Park and support our growing surrounding community. The high school will accommodate up to 800 students, with the capacity to later increase to 1,000 students.

Only last month I had the honour of attending a topping-out ceremony to mark the significance of the delivery of Edmondson Park High School, with the building's structural phase now complete. The project is scheduled to be completed by day one, term 1 of 2027. I thank my community for their patience as the project progresses, and I know what a difference it will make for so many families. I also take this opportunity to thank my Federal colleague Ms Anne Stanley, MP, the member for Werriwa, for another great local community campaign. We have worked together to ensure that our community gets our fair share. The Labor Government will continue the important job of building a better New South Wales for all.

tree_branches.name: Josh Addo-Carr
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Private Members' Statements > Josh Addo-Carr
tree_branches.text:
Lachie was urgently transferred to John Hunter Children's Hospital, and for Jess and Adam, life was turned upside down. A week later, at the Macleay Valley Mustangs Indigenous Round, one of Lachie's best mates met someone he looks up to: Josh Addo-Carr. As a pure Parramatta fan, who comes from a diehard Parramatta family, Lleyton's hero was right there in front of him. I am proud to say that in that moment, while I was at an event, my youngest boy, Lleyton, had the foresight and courage to ask a footballing superstar to look in on his mate. On his way back to Sydney, after a long day or so on the road, The Foxx detoured over an hour out of his way to walk into that hospital room at John Hunter hospital. No fanfare, no questions; it was just one man showing up because it mattered. What he gave Lachie was something none of his family had seen that day: a smile of happiness and shock.

That is what true leadership looks like, and yet stories like this rarely make national news. Too often, footy players are portrayed in the worst light. As humans, sometimes they make mistakes, misbehave or have off-field, real life problems. Often it is not all factual but perceived. On this occasion it is not the full story. This is a positive story not created by the Foxx for publicity, but as a result of a request from a kid looking out for his mate at a country footy ground. In country towns like mine, footy players are heroes. For many of our country kids, playing footy is the dream. The footy stars show up on the kids' school ovals, sign their footy boots that have been worn thin from backyard practice and shake their hands. Kids idolise the players they watch on TV.

Josh Addo-Carr went out of his way to show up for a sick boy he had never met at the request of another young fan. He even tried to recruit him to become a Parramatta fan. His heartfelt effort gave Lachie some joy during his unknown fight. We need role models like Josh who show our young people that leadership is more than skill—it is service. Having a representative like him is powerful, especially for Indigenous kids. Josh is the founder of JAC Academy, a not-for-profit organisation dedicated to empowering Indigenous youth through education, cultural awareness, mental health programs and footy. He is also a director of NDIGI Group, an Indigenous labour hire company that is creating jobs, opening doors and building long-term stability for Indigenous people. He is not just playing the game, he is building a legacy grounded in lifting others and celebrating Aboriginal culture. For that, I give a massive thank you to the Foxx. I thank him for the boots he signs, the hands he shakes, the hope he brings, the examples he sets and for the awesome experience he has given Lachie.

Lachie and his family are experiencing something no family could ever imagine. His parents, Jess and Adam, have shown extraordinary strength, and in the face of fear they have stayed grounded in love and courage, supported by the strength of the community around them. When Lachie's news spread through Smithtown, the community rallied. There was a fundraiser at the oval and a sea of people showed up to support one of their own, buying raffle tickets, cakes and footy jerseys. Standing quietly behind all the stalls were the volunteers, who are the backbone of every footy club. They are the people who make it happen. I thank everyone who turned up to support the family on the day, those who donated money or helped with organising the day. Their generosity is what keeps small towns strong.

I spoke to Lachie and his parents today to confirm that they were still okay for me to deliver this speech tonight, and Jess and Adam asked me to deliver a heartfelt thank you, not only to Josh, but to the Smithtown Tigers community, the volunteers and to all the people who contributed, reached out or developed that special fundraiser. Lachie still has a battle in front of him and there is a way to go. We are behind him every single step of the way. Like the Foxx, he is a strong, young, fast leader amongst his peers. He has the heart of a Tiger. I wish him all the best and I will be there when he makes his comeback.

tree_branches.name: Mr MICHAEL KEMP
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Private Members' Statements > Josh Addo-Carr > Mr MICHAEL KEMP
tree_branches.text: Mr MICHAEL KEMP ( Oxley ) —Since the age of 12, Leyesha Campbell, a proud Dunghutti woman from Kempsey, has faced the realities of kidney disease. Diagnosed with end-stage renal failure as a child, she has undergone dialysis, treatment, and even a transplant - yet she has never let her illness define her. Instead, this extraordinary young woman has turned her experience into a mission to strengthen Aboriginal healthcare. I had the privilege of meeting Leyesha through the NSW Parliament's Young Aboriginal Leaders Program, where she delivered a powerful speech on the urgent need for better health outcomes for Aboriginal people living with kidney disease. Her courage, her determination, and her vision left a deep impression. Through her social platform, Leyesha's Journey, she shares advice, encouragement, and her lived experience. Beyond that, she contributes as a research assistant at the University of Sydney, helping to shape clinical guidelines that ensure care is culturally safe and accessible for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients. Leyesha's story is a reminder that we must do more to deliver world-class healthcare in regional areas. She embodies resilience, leadership, and hope for young people across our communities.

tree_branches.name: Ms JULIA FINN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Private Members' Statements > Josh Addo-Carr > Ms JULIA FINN
tree_branches.text: Ms JULIA FINN ( Granville ) —I acknowledge the unveiling of the NAEOTOM Alpha Pro photon-counting CT scanner at Medscan Merrylands on World Heart Day, 29 September 2025 — a major milestone for healthcare innovation in Western Sydney. Developed by Siemens Healthineers and introduced through Quantum Medscan and Heartscan Australia, this world-leading imaging technology delivers unprecedented clarity in cardiac diagnostics, reduces radiation exposure, and allows for earlier, safer, and more accurate diagnosis of heart disease. It is only the second installation of its kind in NSW, and it will be bulk billed to ensure local patients have equitable access to cutting-edge healthcare. This technology represents a leap forward for preventive medicine and will directly benefit communities in Western Sydney, where rates of heart disease remain among the highest in the state. I commend Dr John O'Rourke, Chris Munday, and the Medscan team for their vision, collaboration, and commitment to improving cardiac health outcomes for all. This is an extraordinary achievement for our local area — bringing world-class innovation home to Western Sydney.

tree_branches.name: Liverpool City Council
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Private Members' Statements > Liverpool City Council
tree_branches.text:
These contributions, together with evidence of prohibited developer donations, raise serious questions about the transparency and legitimacy of these funds, questions that demand the attention of the NSW Electoral Commission, the Independent Commission Against Corruption and this very Parliament. It is incumbent upon integrity agencies to follow the money, trace the source of these donations and determine whether they are legitimate and lawful or being used to disguise the influence of prohibited donors. Straw donations are not only improper; they are unlawful.

If these funds are found to not be genuine, then multiple local government elections in Liverpool were not fought on a fair playing field. Every candidate who contested those elections and every resident who casted a vote has reason to be seriously concerned. Furthermore, serious questions must be asked of the State Liberal Party. Surely, party officials saw these donations coming in and their unusual nature. Did they ask where the money was coming from? Did they ask whether it complied with the law? Or did they simply accept the cash and look the other way? And, in light of these most recent reports, has the State director taken any further action?

While inquiries and investigations are ongoing, a black cloud hangs over the elected and administrative leaders of the City of Liverpool. That cloud cannot be waved away by pathetic excuses that those involved were novices. It must be addressed directly and without delay. Under section 232 of the Local Government Act 1993, councillors have a legal duty to act honestly, exercise care and prioritise the public interest. The Model Code of Conduct for Local Councils reinforces this, requiring councillors to ensure that their councils act lawfully, ethically and transparently. That duty includes responding to serious integrity concerns and, if necessary, standing the CEO aside during those investigations. Let me very clear: This is not a presumption of guilt. It is a basic standard of governance.

Yet at Liverpool City Council we have seen the opposite. Councillors seeking an extraordinary meeting to debate these matters have faced walkouts, the withdrawal of quorum and legal threats to shut down discussion. The mayor has resorted to lawfare to delay and block a lawful request for an extraordinary meeting and to shut down a basic democratic debate about whether the CEO should be stood aside. That conduct is unacceptable. It undermines the council's legitimacy and mocks this Parliament's demands of local governments. Councils are not private boards; they are public institutions, funded by and accountable to the ratepayers and the community. The way forward is clear. The Electoral Commission must audit these donations and trace their true origin. ICAC must investigate any links between donors, developers and the council's decisions. Given the years-long trail of scandals that have plagued Liverpool City Council and its refusal to act on these latest revelations, this Parliament must now act.

In light of the precedent set by parliamentary inquiries into the council of the City of Canterbury Bankstown and the Hills Shire Council in the last term, it is now incumbent on this Parliament to launch its own inquiry into the serious allegations plaguing Liverpool City Council. This is not an abstract debate; it goes to the core of our democracy. The people of Liverpool deserve confidence that their local government operates with honesty, independence and transparency. The pattern of donations, the evidence before the inquiry and the conduct of key figures raise far too many unanswered questions. Those questions must now be answered, without fear or favour.

tree_branches.name: Ms CHARISHMA KALIYANDA
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Private Members' Statements > Liverpool City Council > Ms CHARISHMA KALIYANDA
tree_branches.text: Ms CHARISHMA KALIYANDA ( Liverpool ) ( 20:14 :15 ): I respond to highlight the serious and concerning issues raised by the member for Leppington in his statement. We share the Liverpool local government area, and I know that many of my constituents and many of the residents of the Liverpool local government area have expressed deep dissatisfaction and disappointment with the shenanigans—if I may frame it that way—that are being reported widely in the media about what has taken place in the council, where residents' concerns are being deprioritised for politicking and lawfare. In this term of government, this Government has made a concerted effort to restore faith in democracy and in government institutions by prioritising accountability. I call on the Opposition to support any actions and any measures taken in this respect as well.

tree_branches.name: Ride4Life Mental Health Awareness
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Private Members' Statements > Ride4Life Mental Health Awareness
tree_branches.text:
In 2023, 3,214 Australians lost their lives to suicide—an average of nine people every day. Men are three times more likely to die by suicide than women, and Indigenous Australians are twice as likely to die by suicide as non‑Indigenous Australians. Most tragically, suicide remains the leading cause of death among young people aged 15 to 24. Much more than numbers, these statistics represent lives, futures and families lost forever. That is why initiatives like Ride4Life Australia are so important. I recently met the incredible Ride4Life team— Louise Ginn, Anna Allum, Sonia Beaden and Rachael Beaden—at Avondale University in Cooranbong, just days before they set off to Perth, from where they would begin their world‑first 4,200‑kilometre ride to Sydney on a quad tandem bike.

I followed their journey closely on social media and, as impressive as their reels, posts and videos looked, it was anything but a smooth ride. The team faced freezing conditions, relentless headwinds, broken spokes, flat tyres, overheating, clunky gears, thick fog and even what they called the "Bermuda Triangle for bicycle tyres", which is otherwise known as the Nullarbor Plain. There they became stranded after losing both tyres to a broken rim and hub. But, true to form, they met each setback with good humour and a can‑do attitude. Their journey had its lighter moments from surprise roadside deliveries of homemade scones to inadvertently triggering a multi‑agency response on day five when, having stopped to pump up a tyre, they were spotted by a busload of travelling mayors, who pulled over to cheer them on—as you do. Somehow that scene was reported as a bus crash with CPR in progress!

While I have no doubt that cycling across the continent on a tandem quad was hard yakka, the real work happened when the team stopped at schools, community events and local organisations to share their experiences and speak openly about mental health and suicide prevention. They highlighted the importance of reaching out, speaking up and having meaningful conversations that truly connect. They nailed home the message that "Every Life Counts" and "Mental Health Matters", championing their ultimate goal of "Zero suicides, it's as simple as that". Through their efforts, the Ride4Life crew raised more than $100,000 for Gotcha4Life—an organisation that develops preventative programs and resources to help Australians access support when they need it most. The Ride4Life journey underscores the urgent need to remove the shame and stigma surrounding mental health, depression and complex diagnoses.

People must know that help is available, recovery is possible, and life can be worth living even in the darkest times. The crew reached their finish line at Bondi on 10 October, where they shared a powerful message: "Always remember how much you are loved and valued, tap into your village and practise your mental fitness daily. Every life counts!" I wish I could have joined them at that time. That message was from Louise, Anna, Sonia and Rachael. I thank them for their extraordinary efforts to raise awareness, inspire hope and remind us all that every life is invaluable. I thank the four women and their support team for what they have just done.

tree_branches.name: Mr GREG PIPER
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Private Members' Statements > Ride4Life Mental Health Awareness > Mr GREG PIPER
tree_branches.text: Mr GREG PIPER ( Lake Macquarie ) —I congratulate the dedicated team of volunteers behind NourishEd Australia on reaching a significant milestone, namely the first anniversary since opening their doors in Toronto. Under the leadership of Directors, Nicholas Cade and Jeremy Eastham, NourishEd has secured it's standing as an essential service in the Lake Macquarie area. Nick and Jeremy volunteer full time to keep the grass roots organisation up, running and growing. Through their open-access pantry, free meal service, community cafe, and library, the NourishEd team have provided food relief, community connection, and dignity to hundreds, if not thousands of people across the region over the past 12 months. NourishEd has not only provided food to fill hungry tummies, but also solace for the lonely, a safe space for the vulnerable and a compassionate ear for anyone doing it tough. Following this amazing progress, their plans for Recovery Groups and Education are destined for success. The success and growth of this service is testament to the passion and dedication of the volunteers. I wish NourishEd a very happy first birthday and look forward to many more years of this hub of help making a real difference in our community.

tree_branches.name: Tatiana Markovic
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Private Members' Statements > Tatiana Markovic
tree_branches.text:
In Pie Week, she baked seafood party pies and a colourful fruity tangram pie. While she finished tenth, she remained steady and resilient. Bread Week proved a highlight: Her blueberry and lemon bagels and her moving showstopper, A Nurse's Life, showcased both the technical skill and the personal storytelling that secured her sixth place. Tropical Week brought vibrant flavours, with tropical daisy tarts and experimental meringue bombs, which again placed Tatiana sixth. During Little and Large Week, Tatiana embraced scale with Childhood Days mini cakes and a striking 1920s apartment block showstopper, and she finished seventh. Her creativity came to the fore in Japan Week, when her raspberry and rose Shokupan buns and matcha-inspired desserts earned her fourth place. In Earth Week, she achieved her season's high point—a chocolate and raspberry cake and an elegant blackforest terrarium showstopper, which placed her second overall.

Finally, in Patisserie Week she produced a homestyle en croute and a spiced Charlotte Russe before being eliminated, finishing the season fourth overall—which is an extraordinary achievement in such a talented field. What made Tatiana stand out was not only her technical ability, but also her warmth and authenticity that she infused into every single bake. Each dish told a story honouring her nursing career, celebrating her culture and expressing her creativity. She reminded us that all baking is not simply about flour, sugar and butter; it is about connection, care and community. Her journey is even more inspiring when you consider that Tatiana is a self‑taught baker. Without formal culinary training, she honed her skills through perseverance, experimentation and countless hours in her own kitchen. That journey resonates with so many of us. It shows what is possible when talent meets dedication and when ambition begins not in a professional school but at home and around the family table.

Beyond the tent, Tatiana continues her work as a practising nurse. Nursing demands compassion, resilience and service to others. Baking is also an act of generosity—an offering of joy, nourishment and creativity. That she embodies both roles speaks volumes about her values. She is someone who gives freely of herself, who balances skill with empathy and who makes the world brighter with both care and creativity. Her colleagues, her friends and her family know that Tatiana's bakes extend far beyond television. She shares them generously at work and in the community, and she also brings her creations to a wider audience through her lnstagram account @tatiana.creates. There she posts not only polished cakes but also works in progress, inspiration boards and glimpses behind the scenes.

Tatiana's social media reflects her generosity, her authenticity and her invitation to others to join her journey. She encourages home bakers to take their own creative risks. To finish fourth overall in The Great Australian Bake Off is no small feat. It places Tatiana among the best amateur bakers that Australia has. Her skill, determination and creativity are just incredible. But more than the rankings, it was the way she carried herself throughout the program—with dignity, kindness, humour and humility—that made her an absolute standout. On behalf of everyone in the Parliament of New South Wales and on behalf of the Shellharbour electorate, I thank Tatiana for representing us so gracefully, for showing us what can be achieved with passion and dedication, and for reminding us that excellence and generosity can go hand in hand. Her journey on The Great Australian Bake Off is only the beginning. We cannot wait to see what she creates next, and we will be cheering her on every step of the way. Congratulations, Tatiana, and thank you.

tree_branches.name: Ms ANNA WATSON
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Private Members' Statements > Tatiana Markovic > Ms ANNA WATSON
tree_branches.text: Ms ANNA WATSON ( Shellharbour ) —I would like to acknowledge and congratulate Amanda Kowalczyk from Koonawarra Public School on receiving the Secretary's Award for Excellent Service. Amanda's tireless dedication and outstanding contributions to her school community have made a lasting impact on students, staff, and families alike. Her professionalism, compassion, and unwavering commitment to public education are truly commendable. This award is a reflection of her leadership and the care she brings to her role each day. On behalf of the Shellharbour electorate, I would congratulate Amanda on her amazing work and for being awarded the Secretary's Award for Excellent Service. The recognition is so well deserved, and I know the entire electorate joins me in celebrating her success.

tree_branches.name: Sydney Metro
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Private Members' Statements > Sydney Metro
tree_branches.text:
Sydney Metro records a customer satisfaction rate of 98 per cent and operates with 99.8 per cent on-time running. Reliability and punctuality have made the metro the most dependable mode of transport in Sydney. The jury citation for the NSW Architecture Medallion at the NSW Architecture Awards described the Sydney Metro City and Southwest project as a "new benchmark" for public ambition, stating:

"Legacy project," "city shaping," "world class"- these are phrases often used and too often empty rhetoric. In this case, they are well deserved. The project is transformative, not just in transport terms but in how it redefines civic experience in Sydney.

That is the standard we should set. It has boosted skills and driven urban renewal around station precincts, driving housing, business investment and local vibrancy. Despite this success, the Minns Government has failed to invest in any new metro projects of its own. Every project now under construction—Sydney Metro West, Western Sydney Airport line and the south-west conversion—were decided, designed and commenced under the Coalition. This Government has no future vision and no expansion plan. That lack of ambition risks squandering the momentum the Coalition built. The skilled workforce that has delivered those projects will disperse if the pipeline dries up, and rebuilding that expertise later will be costly and difficult.

Sydney is growing rapidly and needs bold forward planning. The extension of the Western Sydney Airport line to Macarthur and the extension on the Tallawong-St Marys corridor should be accelerated to connect the fast‑growing communities in Western Sydney, support economic development and ease congestion. I have been calling for peak services every three minutes on the M1 line to address overcrowding, particularly in my electorate at Crows Nest, and to meet rising demand. That need is a testament to the metro's popularity and the commuter's desire for efficient, reliable transport options.

A city of Sydney's size and global status cannot afford to stand still when it comes to public transport investment. Labor has called the metro a "vanity project". Perhaps that is no surprise, for Labor's history is clear. It delivered half a rail line when last in office despite promising 12 lines. This time around it will promise no new infrastructure of its own, content with cutting ribbons on Liberal projects. Frankly, Labor in New South Wales has never shown the capacity, nor the competence, to build new major public transport projects. It delayed Sydney Metro West by two years, seeking a pretext to cancel it entirely. Its own review confirmed its necessity and benefits yet it is clear that Labor has never really supported the ambition of the metro. It announced two extra stations on the west line with much fanfare, but that has come to naught. The Premier said:

One of the knocks on the Labor Party in the past is that we put out four, five, six, seven plans for new public transport infrastructure and delivered none of them ... well, I'm just determined not to make that mistake again.

Instead, Chris Minns promises to do absolutely nothing beyond that which is already well underway. That is certainly an easy promise to keep—no question—but it is also a recipe for stagnation and lost opportunity, one which will see us fall behind. It is such a testament to the lack of vision this Premier and his Government has. We are also hearing that Sydney Metro West will be delivered as a stripped-back, no‑frills line, with cuts to station design. Western Sydney deserves stations of the same quality as those in the CBD, not a cheaper, second-class version of this world-class project.

Sydney Metro is economic, social and environmental infrastructure that supports liveability, drives housing supply in well-connected precincts and gives families back precious time. We have seen what happens when governments fail to plan: infrastructure lags, roads choke with traffic and confidence erodes. We cannot repeat those mistakes. I urge the Government to fund and fast-track the Macarthur and Tallawong to St Marys extensions; increase peak service delivery on the M1 line to every three minutes; and plan future expansions and keep the metro system growing. We cannot allow short-sightedness to derail the progress we have made. This is about more than transport; it is about the future shape of our city, our economy and our environment. The decisions we make today will determine whether Sydney remains a world-class, liveable city in the decades to come. Sydney Metro is a legacy worth protecting and a future worth building.

tree_branches.text: Mr TIM JAMES ( Willoughby ) —Ms Unity Taylor-Hill has made an outstanding contribution to public education through a decade of leadership at Anzac Park Public School in Cammeray. tree_branches.name: Trades Careers
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Private Members' Statements > Trades Careers
tree_branches.text:
Today I would like to talk about a topic that is normally overlooked and disregarded,

something that is practical and essential for Australia, Trades.

Students are constantly taught that success is found in university and through getting a degree you are able to find fortunate and high paying jobs.

But this denies students who want to get practical and get their hands dirty, in most cases trades are treated like a backup plan rather than a proper career you can work towards.

Australia is a country run by trades and wouldn't be able to function without them. Our cities, roads and most industries need tradies to be the glue that holds them together.

Hear, hear!

Trades like construction, automotive, engineering, etc, are some of the most demanded jobs in Australia yet they are rarely talked about or given importance—

particularly in our high schools. He goes on:

Schools push academic pathways because they are easy to grade and measure such as things like ATAR. On the other hand, Trades offer different and practical knowledge like, real world skills, job security and the opportunity to create a different impact to the community.

I'm not saying this to degrade the importance of jobs acquired through university, but to show that there are opportunities for students that don't fit the academic Mold and that there are various jobs outside of university that can be pursued.

Trades should be held in the same esteem as any other job and should be

seen as a first-choice career. These are not only first choice careers but professions you

can start straight after or even during high school through apprenticeships.

Apprenticeships are one of the most practical pathways available allowing you to earn

while you learn, avoiding all the possible debt from pursuing university.

Not only that but they allow you to gain recognised qualifications and the tool to open your own business to work independently. The implementation of school-based apprenticeships allows students to have a part of the qualification complete by the time they finish year 12.

Choosing a trade is not settling, it's stepping into a career that is dynamic, respected, and essential. Tradespeople have the opportunity to start their own businesses, work independently, and make a visible impact on the world around them.

It's time we stop treating trades as a backup plan and start celebrating them as the backbone of our nation. By elevating the status of trades in our education system and public discourse, we can create a more inclusive and realistic vision of success, one that values all pathways equally and supports every student in finding their place.

To Marcelo's words, I say, "Hear, hear!" I could not agree with him more. While I was a university academic working in that space, I have to say that what started under John Howard—a degrading of our apprenticeships—has had a profound impact on getting young people into those professions, so I am sure that Marcelo will be happy to hear what I say next. The New South Wales Government values our tradies and our apprentices, which is why the 2025-26 budget delivered a record $3.4 billion investment into trades and skills funding. We know that tradies are the backbone of our economy, even though we have a shortage. We want people to know that those are high-value jobs. People can be supported to get their TAFE degree. Marcelo and every young person finishing year 12 should think about learning a trade at TAFE. They are valued, well-paid jobs. University is not the only option.

tree_branches.name: Community Preschools
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Private Members' Statements > Community Preschools
tree_branches.text:
Those teachers have exactly the same qualifications and do exactly the same job each day as teachers in the public system. In recent months I have spoken to many educators across not only my electorate of Clarence but also the Northern Rivers. They are deeply distressed that they need to take action tomorrow. They feel deeply disappointed that the Government is dragging them through a process that other sectors do not need to go through. They are deeply upset that tomorrow they will need to close their community-based not-for-profit schools. Tomorrow grandparents, neighbours and anyone with spare time will be called to babysit while mums and dads go to work because, across the Northern Rivers, up to 40 not-for-profit preschools that are part of the Northern Rivers Preschool Alliance will shut their doors for a full or half day. I stand in support of those hardworking teachers and staff as they come to Macquarie Street tomorrow.

In a call to arms and a day of action, the protesting educators and some families will march not only in Macquarie Street but also in locations across the Northern Rivers as well. The day of action is to highlight the ongoing battle for funding with the State Government. As I said earlier, the State Government has dragged not‑for‑profit schools through the court system for the past 12 months, and they have frankly had enough. While the Government might not understand the issue playing out in regional New South Wales, it is my job to bring those issues to the Parliament. The sector is experiencing staffing shortages that are growing by the day and will eventually lead to a staffing crisis. Experienced teachers and educators need to leave community preschools to find better paying jobs in the public sector.

As I said, they are doing exactly the same job with exactly the same qualifications, just in a not-for-profit system. Those not-for-profit preschools are also run by dedicated volunteers and boards made up of mums and dads. Whether or not the Government agrees, it has a responsibility to fund the not-for-profit preschool sector. As it stands, the Government is already funding up to 80 per cent of costs. The sector is asking for a very slight increase. Teachers doing exactly the same job in the not-for-profit community sector earn up to 35 per cent less than their colleagues. Not-for-profit community preschools are the safest model of education for preschoolers. They are rated very highly by the Department of Education and exceed the national quality standards. Tomorrow will be a sad day for many of those teachers as they leave the classroom to come to Macquarie Street to protest against the Government.
