tree_branches.name: Coomba and District Progress Association
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Coomba and District Progress Association
tree_branches.text: Mrs TANYA THOMPSON ( Myall Lakes ) —Mr Speaker, I wish to recognise the outstanding achievements of the Coomba Park community and the Coomba and District Progress Association, who were recently honoured at the 2025 Keep Australia Beautiful NSW Tidy Towns Awards. Representing a population of fewer than 1,500 people, Coomba Park achieved remarkable success, being named the 2025 Tidy Town Award Winner. The community also received several major awards, including Winner of the Liveable Towns Award for the Coomba Park Foreshore Half Court, Winner of the Community Spirit and Inclusion Award for the Welcome to Coomba initiative, Winner of the Liveable Towns Award for the Coomba MasterClass, Winner of the Litter Prevention Award for the Butt Bins project, and Winner of the Circular Economy Award for the Recycling Hub. These achievements highlight the strength, creativity, and community spirit that define Coomba Park and demonstrate what can be achieved when a small community works together with a shared purpose. I congratulate the Coomba and District Progress Association and all volunteers involved for their vision and commitment to sustainability and community spirit.

tree_branches.name: Mrs TANYA THOMPSON

tree_branches.text: Mrs TANYA THOMPSON ( Myall Lakes ) —Mr Speaker, I wish to recognise and congratulate Gloria Rowsell for 30 years of dedicated service to education and the Chatham High School community. For three decades, Gloria has been a steady and trusted presence within the school, known fondly as Aunty Gloria by students and staff alike. Her commitment, care, and professionalism have made an enduring impact on generations of young people across our region. Gloria's passion for education and her tireless support of both students and colleagues exemplify the very best of our public education system. Her wisdom, kindness, and willingness to go above and beyond have enriched the lives of countless members of the Chatham High community. On behalf of the people of Myall Lakes, I extend my sincere gratitude to Gloria for her outstanding contribution and congratulate her on this remarkable milestone of 30 years of service.

tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Belle Property Northern Beaches
tree_branches.text: Mr JAMES GRIFFIN ( Manly ) —Mr Speaker, I would like to congratulate the team at Belle Property Commercial Northern Beaches on being recognised as the number one commercial office nationally across the Belle Property Network. This is a great achievement that speaks to their professionalism, expertise, and commitment to excellence. A special congratulations goes to local legend and champion of small business, Klaudia Brown, who was awarded the top agent nationally for highest transactions - a well-deserved achievement. Beyond their business success, Belle Property Northern Beaches also play a valued role in supporting local charities and fundraising events, strengthening our community in meaningful ways. Congratulations once again.

tree_branches.name: Mr JAMES GRIFFIN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Belle Property Northern Beaches > Mr JAMES GRIFFIN
tree_branches.text: Mr JAMES GRIFFIN ( Manly ) —Mr Speaker, it was both a pleasure and a privilege to host domestic violence charity KYUP! at NSW Parliament recently. I want to particularly acknowledge founder and Manly resident Mel Thomas for her extraordinary leadership in establishing this initiative. KYUP!, which translates from Korean to mean "the spirit of self-protection," empowers young women, supports victims, and takes meaningful action to break the cycle of domestic and family violence at the grassroots level. The event was deeply moving and informative, showcasing the tireless work of individuals and organisations striving to create safer communities. It was inspiring to see such strong support, and I congratulate and thank all who took part, including the award recipients. For those in the Chamber who may not yet be familiar with KYUP!, I encourage you to learn more about this remarkable organisation and the important work they are doing to address the urgent issue of violence against women and children in our communities.

tree_branches.name: Manly Business Chamber 2025-26 Committee
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Manly Business Chamber 2025-26 Committee
tree_branches.text: Mr JAMES GRIFFIN ( Manly ) —Mr Speaker, I recognise the Manly Business Chamber and extend my warm congratulations to the new 2025/26 Executive Committee. With expertise spanning retail, property, hospitality, business, architecture, education, and events, this team brings the knowledge and energy needed to support Manly's small business community. Manly faces ongoing challenges for small businesses, particularly during these colder winter months. From rising costs to outdoor dining fees, the leadership, experience, and commitment of this new executive committee is exactly what our community needs to help businesses navigate these challenges and thrive. I would also like to pay special tribute to Monique Eggeling, Drew Johnson, and Klaudia Brown who have concluded their time with the Chamber. I am advised that together, they have dedicated 36 years to strengthening local businesses and leaving a lasting impact on our community. Congratulations once again to the new executive committee. I look forward to working closely with them to support our local entrepreneurs and ensure Manly remains a hub for all things small business.

tree_branches.name: Terrigal Rugby Club – Grand Final Victory
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Terrigal Rugby Club – Grand Final Victory
tree_branches.text: Mr ADAM CROUCH ( Terrigal ) —I acknowledge and congratulate the Terrigal Rugby Club on their thrilling victory in the 2025 Premier 1 Grand Final. On September 30th, Terrigal overcame a determined Razorbacks side in a dramatic 36–34 finish that had the entire Central Coast on the edge of their seats. This was more than just a sporting achievement—it was a moment of community pride and unity. The team showed exceptional skill, resilience, and heart, embodying the very best of grassroots sport. Behind the players is a network of dedicated coaches, volunteers, families, and supporters who have nurtured the club's culture over many years. Sport brings people together, teaches discipline and teamwork, and builds lifelong friendships. The Terrigal Rugby Club is a shining example of these values. Their win was not only well-earned but also a testament to the strength and vibrancy of our local community. To the players, coaching staff, committee members, and fans—I offer my sincere congratulations. Your hard work and determination have made Terrigal proud.

tree_branches.name: Mr ADAM CROUCH
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Terrigal Rugby Club – Grand Final Victory > Mr ADAM CROUCH
tree_branches.text: Mr ADAM CROUCH ( Terrigal ) —I would like to acknowledge the passionate volunteers and organisers behind the Terrigal Repair Café, a community-led initiative that is quietly transforming how we think about waste, sustainability, and connection. Operating regularly in Terrigal, the Repair Café offers local residents the chance to bring in broken household items—jewellery, clothing, electronics, tools—for repair, often with guidance to learn how to fix them themselves. It's a place where sustainability meets community spirit. Visitors don't just leave with a repaired item—they leave with skills, knowledge, and connection. Beyond its practical impact, the Repair Café fosters inclusion and wellbeing. It offers coffee, cake, even wood-fired pizza, turning sustainability into a shared, welcoming experience. In a time when we are grappling with rising costs and environmental challenges, this grassroots initiative is a beacon of community leadership. It reduces waste, strengthens neighbourly ties, and empowers people to value what they already have. To every volunteer fixer, organiser, and participant—thank you. Your work is not only practical but profoundly hopeful. Terrigal and the wider Central Coast are better for it.

tree_branches.name: Lily Rance
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Lily Rance
tree_branches.text: Mr ADAM CROUCH ( Terrigal ) —I would like to take this opportunity to congratulate Lily Rance, a remarkable young achiever from Erina High School, who has been named 2025 Hunter & Central Coast School‑based Apprentice/Trainee of the Year. Lily has completed a Certificate III in Health Services Assistance, trained by TAFE NSW and employed by Hunter New England Local Health District at Belmont Hospital. Her dedication, compassion, and commitment to learning have set her apart as a rising star in the healthcare field. Lily's school‑based traineeship has not only equipped her with clinical and interpersonal skills but also allowed her to support patients during their most vulnerable moments. Combining real-world experience with structured study, she has developed confidence, critical thinking, and leadership—becoming someone her team can rely on. With a strong desire to make a positive impact, Lily is already contributing meaningfully to her community. Her journey is only just beginning, and we look forward to seeing the difference she will continue to make. Congratulations, Lily.

tree_branches.text: Mrs TANYA DAVIES ( Badgerys Creek ) —I congratulate Glenmore Park local Brooklyn Kershaw on winning the Performing Arts-Junior category award of the 2025 Nepean/Blue Mountains Young Champions Awards, held at St Marys Rugby League Club. This achievement was in recognition of Brooklyn's dedication across the fields of Theatre, Drama, Music, Dance, and Public Speaking. I commend Brooklyn for the many hours and great effort she dedicates towards her rehearsals, performances and competitions, it is fitting that she has been recognised with a prestigious award. On behalf of my electorate of Badgerys Creek, I congratulate Brooklyn Kershaw on her outstanding success thus far and wish her continued success ahead.

tree_branches.name: Mrs TANYA DAVIES
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Brooklyn Kershaw > Mrs TANYA DAVIES
tree_branches.text: Mrs TANYA DAVIES ( Badgerys Creek ) —I commend and congratulate Kris Hudswell on her retirement as the Principal of Blackwell Public School, after 25 years of distinguished service in this role. Her retirement coincided with her birthday of 25 August 2025. Mrs Hudswell's exceptional dedication to the education and development of her students leaves a lasting impact and her legacy will remain. One of her many initiatives included the Blackwell Buddies group, which is a precursor to kindergarten and is a 10-week program where local children who are scheduled to attend Blackwell Public School the following year for kindergarten can experience the school. On behalf of my electorate of Badgerys Creek, I thank Mrs Hudswell for her outstanding service to her students and the school community, and I wish her the very best in the next chapter of her life.

tree_branches.name: Clairgate Public School Dancers
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Clairgate Public School Dancers
tree_branches.text: Mrs TANYA DAVIES ( Badgerys Creek ) —I commend and congratulate 10 young dancers from Clairgate Public School for winning and being declared state champions at the Australian All Star Cheerleading Federation State Championships held at Quaycentre on 13 September 2025. The team also won the Grand Champion title, which is awarded to the highest placed school groups across public, private, primary and high schools in any dance style. The 10 dancers from Clairgate Public School ranged from Year 4 to Year 6 and they had been working on their routine since April 2025. Their victory is testament to their hard work and dedication. On behalf of my electorate of Badgerys Creek, I congratulate our victorious dancers and all who supported them and wish them continued success in the future.

tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Cronulla Public School
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK SPEAKMAN ( Cronulla ) —I was delighted to join the Cronulla Public School community last month to mark 100 years on the school's Burraneer Bay Road site. It was an opportunity for past and present students, families and staff to celebrate public education at the beautiful location where its iconic building has been a focal point since the school – now 115-years-old - moved from what is now Monro Park. More important than the bricks and mortar, of course, is the legacy of knowledge and skills imparted, and character built, over many generations - and the continuing commitment to knowledge, skills and the character for future generations. The school's rich history was on display through photos and records, before everyone came together for a special school assembly. I acknowledge principal Trent Bridgland and his wonderful team for the fitting celebration and what they do every day. A special mention to student leaders Summer Ransom, Dallas Towers, Will Green and Boston Highland for hosting the assembly and doing their school proud. Thousands of families are thankful for the learning, fun times and friendships built on the site and vision to locate the school in its idyllic spot.

tree_branches.text: Mr RYAN PARK ( Keira — Minister for Health, Minister for Regional Health, and Minister for the Illawarra and the South Coast ) —Dharawal Distilling Co was celebrated at the 2025 Illawarra Business Awards taking out the top prize in the Outstanding New Business category. To be recognized at this top level is a true testament to the vision, passion, and hard work that goes into running a successful business. The Keira Electorate is filled with many amazing local and family businesses that continue to support our community by creating local jobs, bringing people together and adding to the character of our home. I'd like to extend my congratulations to the team at Dharawal Distilling Co for creating a product that brings together Indigenous culture and Australian botanicals. Your remarkable efforts are a source of great pride for our whole community and will no doubt inspire others to follow your lead in honouring culture, entrepreneurship, community connection and creativity. This success not only shines a spotlight on the Illawarra region but also strengthens our local economy and cultural identity.

tree_branches.name: Scott Westcott
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Scott Westcott
tree_branches.text: Ms JODIE HARRISON ( Charlestown — Minister for Women, Minister for Seniors, and Minister for the Prevention of Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault ) —It was a night of celebration as the Hunter sporting community gathered to honour five outstanding athletes at the 2025 Hunter Region Sporting Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony, held at McDonald Jones Stadium on Wednesday, 20 August. Among the inductees was Scott Westcott, whose commitment to sport and the Hunter community has left a lasting impression. Since beginning his teaching career in 1998, Scott has managed to balance life as an educator with success as an elite athlete. He has proudly represented Australia at the 1998 Chiba International Relay, achieved a fourth-place finish in the 2006 Commonwealth Games Marathon, and competed in the Rio 2016 Olympic Marathon. Scott's passion for athletics extends far beyond his own achievements. He has played an important role in nurturing local talent through his work with the Macquarie Hunter Athletics Club, Newcastle Runners Athletics Club, and the Hunter Academy of Sport. He now leads the athletics program at Hunter Sports High School, inspiring young people to strive for their personal best. Scott Westcott's induction into the Hunter Region Sporting Hall of Fame is a fitting tribute to an athlete, teacher, and mentor who continues to give so much to his community.

tree_branches.name: Ms JODIE HARRISON
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Scott Westcott > Ms JODIE HARRISON
tree_branches.text: Ms JODIE HARRISON ( Charlestown — Minister for Women, Minister for Seniors, and Minister for the Prevention of Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault ) —The Hunter Breast Cancer Foundation has been recognised as the 2025 Business Hunter Award recipient for Outstanding Community Organisation, proudly sponsored by BHP. Since its founding in 1999, the Hunter Breast Cancer Foundation [HBCF] has provided essential, practical support to local residents navigating a breast cancer diagnosis. The organisation offers transport to treatment, cleaning and lawn care services, wigs and headwear, comfort items, and survivorship programs, all completely free of charge. Entirely locally funded, HBCF's small and dedicated team, supported by their ever‑growing Pink Army of volunteers, work tirelessly to ensure that no one in the Hunter faces breast cancer alone. Every dollar raised stays right here in our community, providing vital assistance to Hunter families when they need it most. This well-deserved recognition highlights HBCF's extraordinary impact and the compassion that underpins their work. For more than two decades, they have brought hope, dignity, and care to countless local residents. Congratulations to the Hunter Breast Cancer Foundation on this achievement and for their continued commitment to making a difference in the lives of Hunter families affected by breast cancer. Their dedication is a true reflection of the strength and generosity of our region.

tree_branches.name: Bradley Dunn
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Bradley Dunn
tree_branches.text: Ms JODIE HARRISON ( Charlestown — Min ister for Women, Minister for Seniors, and Minister for the Prevention of Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault ) —It is a privilege to recognise Bradley Dunn, CEO of the Lake Macquarie and Newcastle Suicide Prevention Network, who has been named as one of three finalists for the 2025 Mental Health Commission of NSW's Individual Community Champion Award. For more than 16 years, Brad has dedicated himself to improving mental health outcomes across our region. As CEO, he works tirelessly to secure funding, strengthen partnerships, and ensure the community's voice is heard in shaping mental health services. His leadership has driven several key initiatives, including the rollout of the Shifting the Landscape Strategic Framework, the Navigating the Landscape forum and report, and the launch of National Hope Week, a national campaign promoting suicide prevention and community connection. This year, Brad also spearheaded the creation of the Evolve Mental Health & Wellbeing Hub in Charlestown. The Hub provides a safe, free, and welcoming space where anyone can seek guidance and support for mental health, relationship, or life challenges. Brad's compassion, leadership, and unwavering commitment have transformed countless lives. His recognition as a finalist is a well-deserved honour for someone who continues to make an extraordinary difference in the mental health and wellbeing of our community.

tree_branches.name: Grafton Netball U17s
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Grafton Netball U17s
tree_branches.text: Mr RICHIE WILLIAMSON ( Clarence ) —Congratulations must go to the Grafton Netball U17s team for being crowned Division 3 State Champions at the 2025 HART Senior State Titles in Western Sydney in June. Competing against top ranked teams from across New South Wales, the Grafton players showcased their exceptional skills, focus and strong teamwork, winning a remarkable 14 out of 15 games over the three-day event. Coach Amy Jones must also be congratulated, as she successfully guided the players to become a well‑connected and determined team. A strong start meant that the team lead the ladder on the first day. Despite a narrow one‑point loss to Queanbeyan on day two, they maintained a strong goal percentage and reclaimed the top position on day three with a win over Kiama. With three teams just one point behind them, Grafton steamed ahead to progress through the final day undefeated and took out the title. Goal Attack Ashlea Blair displayed many standout performances throughout the games. The teams sponsors Big River Gym and Fit For Sport also ensured the players were well supported for the competition. Fantastic efforts team – well done!

tree_branches.name: Mr RICHIE WILLIAMSON

tree_branches.text: Mr RICHIE WILLIAMSON ( Clarence ) —I acknowledge the incredible success of this year's Brooms to Bowlo Charity Day for Cystic Fibrosis, organised by Raine & Horne Maclean, Yamba and Iluka, together with the Yamba Bowling Club. On Sunday 3 August, the community once again rallied in a sea of red, walking from Brooms Head to Yamba and gathering at the Bowlo for a day of fundraising and fellowship. This year's event raised $22,292, bringing the total funds raised since 2008 to an extraordinary $133,000+ in support of Cystic Fibrosis Australia. The day was made possible thanks to the dedication of the organising team, the generosity of 67 local businesses and families, and the many volunteers who gave their time to ensure the event's smooth running. From the stunning 23-kilometre walk through Yuraygir National Park, to the family fun, raffles, auctions and entertainment, the Clarence Valley community showed once again what can be achieved when it walks together for a cause that touches so many lives. I congratulate Raine & Horne, Yamba Bowling Club, and everyone who took part in this remarkable day. Your efforts not only raised vital funds but showcased the true heart of our community.

tree_branches.name: Maclean Patchwork & Quilters
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Maclean Patchwork & Quilters
tree_branches.text: Mr RICHIE WILLIAMSON ( Clarence ) —I acknowledge the incredible generosity and community spirit of the Maclean Patchwork and Quilters, who have once again demonstrated their commitment to local healthcare by donating $4000 to the Maclean Hospital Auxiliary. This latest contribution will assist in the purchase of vital diagnostic equipment, including a slit eye lamp and ECG machine, critical tools that will directly benefit patients and staff at Maclean District Hospital. Over the past three years, this dedicated group has raised and donated an outstanding $10,000 to the Hospital Auxiliary, funds that have gone toward upgrading the Palliative Care ward and purchasing essential medical equipment. Their annual "Airing of the Quilts" event, held over Easter, not only showcased the members' remarkable creativity and craftsmanship, but also united the community in support of a great cause. The event's growing popularity has also seen membership increase, breathing new life into the group's already rich 36-year history. I commend President Neil Jackman and Publicity Officer Allison Merrin and all the members of the Maclean Patchwork and Quilters – including founder Wilga Bolton – for their dedication, care, and generosity. You are a shining example of what community spirit looks like in action.

tree_branches.name: Headspace Chatswood New Centre Launch
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Headspace Chatswood New Centre Launch
tree_branches.text: Mr MATT CROSS ( Davidson ) —On Friday 3 October 2025, I joined members of our local community to officially re-open headspace Chatswood at its new home on 465 Victoria Avenue. headspace provides mental health and wellbeing support to young people aged 12 to 25. As part of headspace day 2025, the launch brought together local young people, families and representatives from the Sydney North Local Health District to celebrate community and the importance of mental health. The new centre offers a welcoming, modern space designed to connect young people with the help they need in a safe and inclusive environment. Thank you to the headspace Chatswood team for their ongoing dedication to supporting young people and for giving our community hope, connection and support. I recognise the work of local constituent Lisa Brown, who is an accredited mental health social worker, for her commitment to headspace. I am proud to eagerly support their work in the Parliament of NSW.

tree_branches.name: Mr MATT CROSS
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Headspace Chatswood New Centre Launch > Mr MATT CROSS
tree_branches.text: Mr MATT CROSS ( Davidson ) —I recognise the leadership of Melissa Brown as Principal of Covenant Christian School from 2020 to 2025. I have visited Covenant Christian School on several occasions and have seen firsthand the supportive and inclusive environment Mrs Brown has fostered. She is well respected from all aspects of our local community, including students, teachers, staff and volunteers. During her six years of service, Mrs Brown has guided the school with a vision underpinned by a Christ-centred educational framework that equips students academically and for lifelong success to help them become confident and well-rounded. We thank Mrs Brown for her faithful service and wish her every success as she continues her PhD studies and future endeavours. I am proud to recognise outstanding leaders like Melissa Brown who inspire the future of education. Thank you for your public service to our community.

tree_branches.name: Upper North Shore Volunteer of the Year Awards 2025
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Upper North Shore Volunteer of the Year Awards 2025
tree_branches.text: Mr MATT CROSS ( Davidson ) —On Friday 19 September 2025, I attended the Upper North Shore Volunteer of the Year Awards. These awards celebrate the selfless contributions of individuals and teams who strengthen and support our community. It was an honour to attend and congratulate this year's award recipients: Upper North Shore Volunteer: Glenn Bridgland from Little Wings. Young Volunteer: Max Harpham from The Shepherd Centre. Adult Volunteer: Declan O'Hare from Justice Advocacy Service. Emergency Volunteer: John Aitken from Marine Rescue NSW. Volunteer Team: Street Side Medics. Each of these volunteers has made an extraordinary difference to society: flying children to critical treatment, mentoring young people with hearing loss, supporting clients with disabilities in the justice system, keeping our waterways safe, and providing medical care to people experiencing homelessness. Thank you to all volunteers for the time and compassion they dedicate to our community. I am proud to recognise their service in the Parliament of NSW and will continue to eagerly support volunteers across the Upper North Shore.

tree_branches.name: Mavis Barnes – Part of Kendall's Heartbeat
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Mavis Barnes – Part of Kendall's Heartbeat
tree_branches.text: Mr ROBERT DWYER ( Port Macquarie ) —I rise to recognise the immense contribution to the Kendall community. Mavis Barnes, now aged 91, and still living in Kendall, has selflessly given her time and energies for the betterment of the place she calls home. I understand that Mavis's involvement has spanned more than 60 years. This is a miraculous devotion, and I sincerely thank Mavis for her years of community charity. I believe that Mavis has only recently retired from her position of Secretary of the Kendall National Violin Competition Committee, the competition being one of Australia's foremost performance opportunities for young violinists who are citizens or residents of Australia. This competition has been running since 1999 and we all know that ongoing major events of this significance do not just happen, they come to fruition through shared vision and solid commitment of those who believe in the cause. Mavis has also been an active supporter of the Kendall Community Centre Trust. On the community Centre's web page it states that "Kendall is a community with a heartbeat." Mavis, we thank you for everything you have contributed during your lifetime to the community spirit and achievements of vibrant Kendall.

tree_branches.name: Mr ROBERT DWYER
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Mavis Barnes – Part of Kendall's Heartbeat > Mr ROBERT DWYER
tree_branches.text: Mr ROBERT DWYER ( Port Macquarie ) —I rise to recognise David Castleton, a driving force behind the growth and success of the Queens Lake Sailing Club for over two decades. Since joining as a junior sailor in 1997, David has demonstrated unwavering commitment to the sport and the community. His early advocacy saw sailing introduced as a school sport, personally providing boats and mentoring students. In 2013, David joined the committee, securing vital grants to upgrade safety equipment and improve accessibility for volunteers. He also championed junior development, enabling many young sailors to obtain their boat licences. As Commodore since 2015, David led the club through a period of remarkable growth, hosting state and national titles, expanding the fleet of club-owned boats, and launching inclusive 'Try Sailing' programs for all ages and abilities. His leadership saw the removal of hazardous debris from the lake, enhancing safety for all users. David's vision culminated in the successful extension of the clubhouse, providing essential boat storage and supporting family participation. His dedication is evident, from morning sailing sessions to competitive afternoon races, bridging generations with a 70-year age gap among sailors. David's legacy is one of inclusion, opportunity and enduring community spirit.

tree_branches.name: Port Macquarie U3A 20th Anniversary
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Port Macquarie U3A 20th Anniversary
tree_branches.text: Mr ROBERT DWYER ( Port Macquarie ) —I congratulate the Port Macquarie University of the Third Age, or U3A celebrating its 20th Anniversary in 2025. The University of the Third Age, familiarly called U3A, began in France in 1973 and in Australia in 1984. The Port Macquarie Hastings branch was established in 2005. Now with over 500 members it is a strong member based organisation in our community. Anyone aged 50 years and over, retired or semi-retired can join. Members meet in a warm and friendly environment to learn from each other about topics including history, art, music, languages, movies, drama, dancing, yoga, crafts and health. It is all about fun and learning, no exams, no homework. U3A members also enjoy social activities including Melbourne Cup event, trivia, excursions and other celebrations.. U3A is entirely run by volunteers offering opportunities to socialise, share interests, and keep mentally and physically active and healthy. Its executive committee of President Karen Roberts, Vice President Chris Taylor, Secretary Sue Moll and Treasurer Simon Abell are well supported by Committee members Mike Rogers, Jane Stevenson, Cathy Rasmussen, Alison Williamson, Carol Baker and Lorraine Beukers. I congratulate U3A Port Macquarie on your great contribution to our community.

tree_branches.text: Mr ROBERT DWYER ( Port Macquarie ) —I rise to recognise David Castleton, a driving force behind the growth and success of the Queens Lake Sailing Club for over two decades. Since joining as a junior sailor in 1997, David has demonstrated unwavering commitment to the sport and the community. His early advocacy saw sailing introduced as a school sport, personally providing boats and mentoring students. In 2013, David joined the committee, securing vital grants to upgrade safety equipment and improve accessibility for volunteers. He also championed junior development, enabling many young sailors to obtain their boat licences. As Commodore since 2015, David led the club through a period of remarkable growth, hosting state and national titles, expanding the fleet of club-owned boats, and launching inclusive 'Try Sailing' programs for all ages and abilities. His leadership saw the removal of hazardous debris from the lake, enhancing safety for all users. David's vision culminated in the successful extension of the clubhouse, providing essential boat storage and supporting family participation. His dedication is evident, from morning sailing sessions to competitive afternoon races, bridging generations with a 70-year age gap among sailors. David's legacy is one of inclusion, opportunity and enduring community spirit.

tree_branches.name: Marist Brothers Rams Win First-Ever NRRRL Premiership
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Marist Brothers Rams Win First-Ever NRRRL Premiership
tree_branches.text: Ms JANELLE SAFFIN ( Lismore — Minister for Small Business, Minister for Recovery, and Minister for the North Coast ) —I wish to congratulate the Marist Brothers Rams on winning their first‑ever NRRRL Premiership, and their first grand final win in 22 years. The Rams defeated the Murwillumbah Mustangs 20‑12 in a thrilling grand final at Lismore's Crozier Field. Rams coach Darryl Butcher told The Lismore App that 13 of the 17 players on field were local juniors who had come up through the ranks in the past three years. "It's something that I'm really proud of, because I've done a lot of coaching through juniors," Butcher said. Victory was sweet for Rams veterans, including Co-Captains Paul O'Neill Junior and Mitchell Krause, and Lennon Bartlett. Paul O'Neill Junior said that Lismore has always been a really strong sporting town, particularly for rugby league. "The town itself has been through a lot in the last few years, so this is something that everyone can celebrate a little bit, enjoy themselves and have a good time." I also congratulate the Marist Brothers Ramettes who finished runners-up to Tweed Seagulls in the Ladies League Tag (12-10) and the Northern United Ladies Tackle Team who won their Premiership with a resounding 44-6 win over the Bilambil Jets.

tree_branches.name: Ms JANELLE SAFFIN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Marist Brothers Rams Win First-Ever NRRRL Premiership > Ms JANELLE SAFFIN
tree_branches.text: Ms JANELLE SAFFIN ( Lismore — Mini ster for Small Business, Minister for Recovery, and Minister for the North Coast ) —I wish to congratulate the team at Priceline Pharmacy in Lismore Square on an impressive list of state and national awards won recently. These include Store of the Year, State winner; Beauty Advisor of the Year Michelle Le Page, State and National winner; and Sisterhood Foundation Award, State and National winner. Being located so close to the Queensland border, Lismore is included in the Northern NSW/South East Queensland area of Priceline stores. Australia-wide, there are around 470 stores. Lismore Priceline Retail Manager Kristy Paterson told The Lismore App she was so proud of her team's achievements. Winning the Sisterhood Foundation Award was particularly special because the store raised over $30,000 for the eight Sisterhood Foundation charity partners – Jean Hailes for Women's Health, Smiling Mind, Her Herat, Share the Dignity, Fitted for Work, SisterWorks, Perinatal Anxiety and Depression Australia [PANDA] and Motherless Daughters. Kristy said this was achieved through in-store activities, like community days. "So we'll have face painting, nail painting and bake sales that we set up outside the store," Kristy said. Priceline staff bake cakes, biscuits and slices at home. Congratulations to all staff on their service and caring for community.

tree_branches.name: Norco Eat the Street Festival Returns to Lismore's CBD
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Norco Eat the Street Festival Returns to Lismore's CBD
tree_branches.text: Ms JANELLE SAFFIN ( Lismore — Minister for Small Business, Minister for Recovery, and Minister for the North Co ast ) —Thanks to a $292,280 NSW Government grant and corporate sponsorship by NORCO, the popular Eat the Street festival will return to Lismore's Central Business District on Saturday, 15 November, and for two more years thereafter. This is the city of Lismore's signature food, arts and culture festival, and is expected to attract thousands of local residents and visitors. I'm delighted that a grant to Lismore City Council under the Vibrant Streets Package – Open Streets Program 2023-2028, together with NORCO's corporate sponsorship, has made the event possible after a break of four years. The re-launching of Eat the Street represents a big vote of confidence in the future of Lismore. I'll always keep pushing for projects that bring life to our community and help the local economy thrive. From midday to 7pm on 15 November, Keen Street between Magellan and Woodlark streets and the Lismore Quad will be closed to traffic and opened to people. That part of the CBD will come alive with food stalls, pop-up performances, live entertainers and family-friendly activities. NORCO, an iconic dairy co-operative, is the naming rights partner for Eat the Street for the next three years.

tree_branches.name: Double Bay Diamonds
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Double Bay Diamonds
tree_branches.text: Ms KELLIE SLOANE ( Vaucluse ) —I would like to recognise the Double Bay Diamonds who have won the Marie Kelly Club of the Year Award at the 2025 Randwick Netball Association's Awards. With more than 500 players and volunteers, the club fielded 49 teams, including record-breaking 10 Under-10s sides, with 9 reaching finals under the guidance of Head Coach Gabby. Overall, an outstanding 80% of all teams were positioned for finals by Round 13. Over 30 players earned RNA Representative and Development team selection, while 14 competed in the Metro League. Off the court, the Diamonds expanded sponsorships, fundraising, and hardship support, grew social media engagement by 50%, and established the Donna Johanson Award for Resilience. We are so proud to have the Double Bay Diamonds in our community, and this award is recognition of an outstanding club and culture. Congratulations to the board, coaches, players and volunteers on an incredible season.

tree_branches.name: Ms KELLIE SLOANE
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Double Bay Diamonds > Ms KELLIE SLOANE
tree_branches.text: Ms KELLIE SLOANE ( Vaucluse ) —I would like to congratulate Double Bay Sailing Club on their successful Double Bay Regatta held on Saturday 11th October, 2025. This was the inaugural regatta and was open to all ILCA / Laser sailors from Sydney and beyond, with three races held on the single day in Sydney Harbour. The winning sailor from each class had their name inscribed on the Mark Bathwaite Trophy, named after the Double Bay Sailing Club legend. Congratulations to DBSC on a successful event and looking forward to many more in the years to come!

tree_branches.name: 4th Bondi to Manly Ultra
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > 4th Bondi to Manly Ultra
tree_branches.text: Ms KELLIE SLOANE ( Vaucluse ) —I would like to congratulate the organisers and runners in the upcoming 4th Bondi to Manly Ultra. Starting at the famous Bondi Pavilion, the run follows the 80km Bondi to Manly walking track around Sydney Harbour. Runners weave their way along spectacular cliff tops to Watsons Bay then hug the harbour foreshore through national parks, around iconic Australian landmarks and cultural sites, crossing the finish line at Manly Beach. This is one of the most renowned races in the world, with some of the best scenery, and it continues to grow each year. This year they have 3100 runners taking part, with a whopping 900 ultra runners and over 2200 runners taking part in the relay. Congratulations to all the organisers and good luck to all the runners. Make sure you stop your strava at the end!

tree_branches.name: 2025 Business of the Year
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > 2025 Business of the Year
tree_branches.text: Mrs HELEN DALTON ( Murray ) —Speaker, Today I would like to commend Intereach on being named 2025 Business of the Year at the Deniliquin Business Excellence Awards. The organisation also received awards for Excellence in Diversity and Inclusion, and Employer of Choice (21 employees and over) — a reflection of its inclusive values, strong leadership, and the positive culture it fosters for staff and volunteers alike. With deep roots in Deniliquin going back more than 50 years, Intereach now supports communities across regional NSW and Victoria, delivering vital services in areas like aged care, disability support, and family programs. Their recognition for Diversity and Inclusion celebrates ongoing efforts to ensure culturally safe and welcoming spaces, while the Employer of Choice award highlights their commitment to supporting and valuing their people. It was also a proud moment for Intereach chair Rob Brown, who was named Outstanding Business Leader for his dedication to community and steady leadership. Congratulations to the entire Intereach team on this well-deserved recognition from the community where it all began.

tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Shauna Abrahamson
tree_branches.text: Ms YASMIN CATLEY ( Swansea — Minister for Police and Counter-terrorism, and Minister for the Hunter ) —Speaker, I rise to acknowledge Shauna Abrahamson of Redhead Surf Lifesaving Club for her success the 2025 Hunter Surf Lifesaving Awards of Excellence. The Awards acknowledge outstanding performance by individuals and teams, along with the contribution of administrators. In the Hunter we have some truly amazing surf lifesaving competitors so these awards are always fiercely contested. This year Shauna Abrahamson of Redhead Surf Lifesaving Club took out Facilitator of the Year in acknowledgement of the fantastic work she does to support the Club. Our surf clubs are at the heart of our community but they are powered by their volunteers and the dedication of the surf lifesavers. We are in debt for the work they do to keep us safe over the summer months and train the next generation to be water safe. Congratulations to Shauna on being named Facilitator of the Year, and thank you also to all the volunteers and surf lifesavers across the Hunter.

tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Shauna Abrahamson > Ms YASMIN CATLEY
tree_branches.text: Ms YASMIN CATLEY ( Swansea — Minister for Police and Counter-terrorism, and Minister for the Hunter ) —Speaker, I rise to acknowledge Daniel Wood of Northlakes High School who participated in the You Should be a Cop program. The You Should Be a Cop program was held at Bateau Bay PCYC and is a 4‑day educational and interactive experience facilitated by the NSW Police Force Youth Command. The program is a free interactive experience between participants and serving Police Officers who will provide advice and mentorship throughout the program. Daniel is completing his HSC (Life Skills) in the Northlakes High School's Adaptive Learning Centre, he also works in the school canteen to gain job readiness skills. Daniel also volunteers with the local RFS and is a founding member of the Northlakes High School Leo Club. It is fantastic to see young community leaders like Daniel look to policing as a future career as they determine what their future holds.

tree_branches.name: Family GP Dr. George Han 21 Years of Service
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Family GP Dr. George Han 21 Years of Service
tree_branches.text: Mr CHR IS MINNS ( Kogarah — Premier ) —I would like to commend Dr George Han on his retirement after his 30-year career as a family doctor in Beverly Hills. Dr Han provided every patient with the utmost care and kindness, being considered a close family member to many residents in the community. Born in Brunei, he completed his medical training in the UK before settling into his forever home, Australia. For the past 21 Years, Dr Han has run a solo practice in Beverly Hills, being a cornerstone of the community. He has been a crucial lifeline for generations of families, being considered the 'peoples champion' by locals in the area. He has aided the community day and night, guiding patients through mental and physical health challenges and saving many lives. Once again, I would like to commend Dr George Han for his 30-year career as a general practitioner and wish him the best for his retirement.

tree_branches.name: Mr CHRIS MINNS
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Family GP Dr. George Han 21 Years of Service > Mr CHRIS MINNS
tree_branches.text: Mr CHRIS MINNS ( Kogarah — Premier ) —I wish to commend the Bexley Podiatry Clinic for their paediatric services across Sydney, and humanitarian efforts around the world. The clinic provides expert and personal care across Sydney, making the effort to visit their patients' homes and support vulnerable patients, the clinic's work extending beyond the local community. Dr Fadel Ghazi and Dr Hasan Hamad participated in a humanitarian mission in Iran during one of the world's largest religious pilgrimages. Alongside other medical professionals, they helped treat 45,000 individuals who had walked long distances and were suffering from foot and leg injuries. They provided immediate relief and restored mobility for thousands who had little to no access to professional healthcare. In Kenya, Dr Vanessa Hadchiti offered her care to the children of a local orphanage, many of whom live with physical disabilities. She provided treatment and support, improving mobility and comfort for the children while giving advice to caregivers to aid with ongoing care. The Bexley Podiatry Clinic and their team have made fantastic contributions across our local community and in the world, and once again I commend them for their great work.

tree_branches.name: Alan Garth Martin 100th Birthday
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Alan Garth Martin 100th Birthday
tree_branches.text: M r CHRIS MINNS ( Kogarah — Premier ) —I would like to congratulate Alan Garth Martin on his 100th birthday. Alan was born in 1925, growing up on his grandparent's Mt Crystal property surrounded by a large family. After school his family moved to Willoughby, where Alan studied at Randwick Technical College for five years, earning an advanced certificate in Marine Engineering. Alan played Rugby League for Souths Juniors Armstrong Holland team and was captain-coach for two years. Alan moved to Mt Isa Mine, spending 8 years at sea as a marine engineer. On 14 September 1957, he married Mary Adele Halpin. When their first daughter was born, Alan continued his engineering career ashore as a building engineer in Gold Fields House at Circular Quay. Retiring at 61, he enjoyed just a year off before returning to work as a consultant building engineer, retiring again at 71. A devoted husband, father and grandfather, Alan has two daughters, three grandchildren and four great-grandchildren. He still lives in the first house he purchased in 1960 and continues to drive. Once again, I would like to congratulate him as he proudly celebrates his 100th birthday—a life marked by hard work, service and deep family connections.

tree_branches.text: Mr DUGALD SAUNDERS ( Dubbo ) —Speaker…… I would like to acknowledge Chris Redfern of Wellington who has recently hung up his firefighting gear for the final time, marking the end of a phenomenal twenty-three years of service to Fire and Rescue NSW. Chris was appointed to the Wellington Brigade on 1 August 2002, as a Retained (On-Call) Firefighter. From that day he consistently provided outstanding service and commitment to ensuring the safety and wellbeing of the Wellington community. Balancing his firefighting duties with establishing his own building business and raising a family, Chris often dropped tools mid-job to respond to emergencies, a true testament to his reliability and sense of duty. Over the years, his exemplary service and conduct have been recognised with the National Medal, Fire and Rescue NSW Long Service and Good Conduct Medal with one clasp. Chris, your contributions have made a meaningful difference in times when your community needed you most, thank you for your courage and steadfast support. Enjoy retirement!

tree_branches.name: Mr DUGALD SAUNDERS
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Chris Redfern > Mr DUGALD SAUNDERS
tree_branches.text: Mr DUGALD SAUNDERS ( Dubbo ) —Speaker…… I would like to acknowledge Karen Quinn, who has recently been inducted as a Life Member of the Mudgee Touch Association. Karen has had a long and dedicated association with Mudgee touch football, taking on many roles and responsibilities over the years. She continues to serve the club today in the important role of Registrar, a position she has holds with pride and commitment. Her outstanding contribution to the club through her time, passion, and tireless efforts, has been instrumental in the success and growth of the association. Karen is known for her reliability, positive attitude, and genuine love for the sport and the people involved in it. In 2017, Karen received the Peter Spinner Club Person of the Year Award, which recognises individuals who bring energy, dedication, and a strong community spirit to the club. Karen's unwavering support continues to have a lasting and meaningful impact on the Mudgee sporting community. Her life membership is a well-deserved recognition of the legacy she has built over many years. Congratulations, Karen, on this well-deserved honour. Sporting clubs simply couldn't operate without volunteers like you. Thank you for everything you have done and continue to do.

tree_branches.name: Jack Newman and Lance Barber
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Jack Newman and Lance Barber
tree_branches.text: Mr DUGALD SAU NDERS ( Dubbo ) —Speaker…… I would like to acknowledge Jack Newman and Lance Barber of Mudgee who have recently returned home from participating in the US Open ISKA World Marital Arts Championships in Florida, an event which drew more than three thousand competitors each day. The Mudgee based duo tested their skills against some of the best fighters in the world and both returned home with excellent results. Jack, owner and head instructor at Mudgee Martial Arts, competed in multiple divisions. His impressive final tally included third in black belt traditional weapons A, third in heavyweight black belt clash sparring, and second in heavyweight black belt point sparring. For 17-year-old Lance, it was an opportunity of a lifetime. Not only was it his first time competing on the world stage, but also his first overseas trip. He took part in four events, securing first place in clash sparring, second in sword combat, fifth in point sparring, and eighth in traditional forms. As Lance's coach, Jack, can be proud of both his own success as a competitor and of guiding Lance to such remarkable results. Congratulations to both Jack and Lance, you have done yourselves and Mudgee proud!

tree_branches.name: Where's Nick Wins Australia's Best Wine Bar List - Fiona Macdonald Award
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Where's Nick Wins Australia's Best Wine Bar List - Fiona Macdonald Award
tree_branches.text: Ms JO HAYLEN ( Summe r Hill ) —I would like to congratulate Where's Nick wine bar in Marrickville, recognised at Australia's Wine List of the Year Awards with the prestigious Fiona Macdonald Award. This achievement honours Where's Nick's exceptional curation of sustainably produced and locally sourced wines. The Fiona Macdonald Award recognises wine bars demonstrating outstanding commitment to quality, sustainability, and supporting local producers – values that define Where's Nick. Founded in 2017 by brothers Julian and Dominic Abouzeid, and joined in 2020 by Bridget Raffal, Where's Nick has become a beloved neighbourhood institution on Marrickville Road, creating a welcoming space where wine enthusiasts and newcomers can explore natural, organic, and biodynamic wines. The venue operates as both wine bar and shop, spreading the joy of discovering exceptional wines. Where's Nick demonstrates that small independent businesses can compete at the highest level while staying true to their values. This award showcases Marrickville's thriving hospitality scene and the passionate operators who make our community vibrant. Congratulations to Bridget, Julian, Dominic and the entire team at Where's Nick on this well-deserved national recognition.

tree_branches.name: Ms JO HAYLEN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Where's Nick Wins Australia's Best Wine Bar List - Fiona Macdonald Award > Ms JO HAYLEN
tree_branches.text: Ms JO HAYLEN ( Sum mer Hill ) —Congratulations to Addison Road Community Centre for winning the prestigious Food for Good award at the Sydney Morning Herald Good Food Guide Awards this week. This honour recognises their unwavering commitment to food justice, sustainability, and community care. Located in Marrickville, Addi Road is a hub of innovation and compassion. From their Food Pantry to their advocacy for equity and inclusion, they continue to uplift the most vulnerable in our community. Under the leadership of CEO Rosanna Barbero, Addi Road has transformed surplus food into dignity and nourishment for thousands, setting a powerful example of grassroots action. However, the real power of Addi Road is the hundreds of volunteers who commit their time and energy to make everything possible. To deliver just the Food Pantry services takes almost 900 volunteers! Winning the Food for Good award is a well-earned recognition of the Centre's impact and the strength of community-led solutions. Congratulations again to Rosanna and the entire Addi Road team‑ you make our community proud.

tree_branches.name: Juno Smith – Road Cycling Success
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Juno Smith – Road Cycling Success
tree_branches.text: Ms JO HAYLEN ( Summer Hill ) —Congratulations to Juno Smith, a Year 9 student at Marrickville High School, whose exceptional performance at the Australian Road Cycling Nationals demonstrates the incredible talent emerging from our local schools. Representing NSW Juno delivered truly remarkable results across three demanding events. Her bronze medal in the Individual Time Trial, competing against 28 riders from across the country, showcased her determination and skill. Not only did she claim third place overall, but she was the fastest NSW rider, edging out fourth place by just 0.6 seconds in a thrilling finish. Her consistent excellence continued in both of her other races in the event, finishing as the fastest NSW rider in both events. What makes Juno's achievements even more impressive is her immediate transition to representing Australia in Japan at the Coupe du Japon Fukukoka International XCO Race, competing alongside just eight other Australian cyclists. Juno's dedication, talent, and sportsmanship reflect the very best of our community. She inspires young people everywhere to pursue their dreams with passion and determination. Congratulations Juno – Marrickville High School and our entire community are incredibly proud of you!

tree_branches.name: Annangrove Public School P&C Movie Night
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Annangrove Public School P&C Movie Night
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK HODGES ( Castle Hill ) —I congratulate the Annangrove Public School P&C Association on the outstanding success of their Community Movie Night, held on 20 September. It was a fantastic evening that brought together around 400 parents, students, and local residents for a fun-filled night of entertainment under the stars. The event was the culmination of months of planning and teamwork, with preparations beginning early in the year. I especially acknowledge P&C President Belinda Milner and Events Coordinator Chantelle Wardini for their leadership and dedication in bringing this ambitious event to life. Their efforts created an unforgettable community celebration — complete with food trucks, games, inflatables, raffles, and entertainment for all ages. The screening of Sing 2 — chosen by popular vote — captured the joyful spirit of the evening. Funds raised will go toward important improvements and new technology for the school, including improving the school sign. This event was a wonderful showcase of community spirit, and I commend the P&C for their tireless commitment to supporting the students and families of the school.

tree_branches.name: Mr MARK HODGES
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Annangrove Public School P&C Movie Night > Mr MARK HODGES
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK HODGES ( Castle Hill ) —I congratulate the Australian Chinese Wushu (Kung Fu) Culture Association Inc. on the outstanding success of the Australia Kung Fu & Tai Chi Festival, held on 20 September 2025 in Castle Hill. It was a pleasure to attend this wonderful celebration, which brought together martial arts masters, families, and community in a spirit of friendship and mutual respect. The festival showcased the grace and discipline of traditional Chinese martial arts. It was inspiring to see so many people of all backgrounds participating, learning, and sharing in the joy of cultural exchange. I particularly wish to acknowledge Yunkuo Wang and Pablo Barreto, the President and Treasurer of the Australian Chinese Wushu (Kung Fu) Culture Association, as well as Vicky Jiang, Festival Host, whose leadership and enthusiasm were central to the event's success. Their dedication to promoting cultural understanding through the arts continues to strengthen community bonds within The Hills and beyond. The festival was a truly uplifting example of culture in action. The festival was a wonderful contribution to our community. The festival allowed our multicultural community to come together to enjoy and celebrate shared cultural, community and friendship.

tree_branches.name: Matthew Perram, Hills Football Inc Life Member
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Matthew Perram, Hills Football Inc Life Member
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK HODGES ( Castle Hill ) —I congratulate Matthew Perram who was on 20 September 2025 awarded a Life Membership of Hills Football. Matt has dedicated decades of service to football. Matt's journey began in 1995, when he first joined Glenhaven FC, the club he has proudly represented for his entire playing career and still does to this very day. In 2013, Matt's passion for the game extended beyond the pitch when he joined the Glenhaven Committee as Club Treasurer. From that point forward, his commitment only grew, taking on numerous roles within the club, most notably serving as Club President from 2015 to 2017, guiding Glenhaven through important years of growth and development. Matt's influence extended beyond Glenhaven when he became an inaugural director of Sydney Hills in 2015, before returning to club responsibilities in 2016. His leadership journey continued in April 2018, when he joined the Hills Football Board. Matt has been instrumental in shaping football in the Hills, serving in key roles such as Director of Judiciary, Director of Finance, and most recently, taking on the esteemed position of Chairperson of Hills Football in 2020. I recognise and congratulate Matt on being awarded a Life Membership

tree_branches.name: Guild Theatre 'secret Bridesmaid's Business' Production
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Guild Theatre 'secret Bridesmaid's Business' Production
tree_branches.text: Mr ST EPHEN KAMPER ( Rockdale — Minister for Lands and Property, Minister for Multiculturalism, Minister for Sport, and Minister for Jobs and Tourism ) —I would like to take this opportunity to recognise and congratulate the Guild Theatre Company, of Walz Street, Rockdale, on the success of their newest production, 'Secret Bridesmaid's Business'. Written by Elizabeth Coleman and directed by Susan Stapleton, 'Secret Bridesmaids' Business' has been praised as a witty, funny, and emotional play that explores themes of trust, betrayal, and the complex nature of human relationships. The success of the play speaks volumes to the fantastic and ongoing contribution of the Guild Theatre to the Rockdale community. Since 1952, the guild has produced more than 250 plays, covering everything from drama and comedy, to classics and musicals. The Guild Theatre has become a staple of the Rockdale community, providing a place for skilled performers to learn and practise their craft, while also providing entertaining evenings for members of the community. The Guild Theatre has a long history of unique and interesting productions, and I have no doubt 'Secret Bridesmaid's Business' is another success story for the theatre. Once again, I thank the Guild Theatre Company for their contribution to the Rockdale community and wish everyone involved the best of luck for their future productions.

tree_branches.text: Mr STEPHEN KAMPER ( Rockdale — Minister for Lands and Prope rty, Minister for Multiculturalism, Minister for Sport, and Minister for Jobs and Tourism ) —I was privileged to recently meet August and Helen to celebrate their 70th wedding anniversary. It was a truly special occasion as August and Helen shared heartfelt stories of their life together, tales of challenges they had overcome, and the deep love that has carried them through seven decades. This celebration was not just about marking a milestone, but honouring a lifetime of shared dreams, resilience, unwavering support and I truly feel honoured to celebrate this occasion with them. Augustus Vasseleu was born in Five Dock, NSW, to Ioannis and Zenobia. Helen Vasseleu was born in Tripolis, Greece, to Dimitri and Maria Kringas. Her childhood was shaped by the trauma of World War II and the Greek Civil War, which disrupted her education and family life. In the early 1950s, Helen and her older sister migrated to Australia, sponsored by uncles, and settled in Bondi. Helen and Augustus met through family connections, raised three children, and now enjoy five grandchildren and one great-grandchild during their fulfilling 70-year marriage. It was a privilege to meet them both and I wish them both the very best.

tree_branches.name: Arncliffe Public School
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Arncliffe Public School
tree_branches.text: Mr STEPHEN KAMPER ( Rockdale — Minister for Lands and Property, Minister for Multiculturalism, Minister for Sport, and Minister for Jobs and Tourism ) —Last month, I had the opportunity to visit Arncliffe Public School and meet with Principal Pamela Ladd. It was truly inspiring to witness firsthand the dedication, professionalism, and care that she and her entire team bring to creating a nurturing and positive learning environment for every student. From the moment I arrived, it was clear that this is a school where students are not only supported academically, but also emotionally and socially. Principal Ladd's commitment to fostering both academic excellence and emotional wellbeing was evident in every corner of the school. From the vibrant, student-centred classrooms to the welcoming, engaging outdoor learning spaces. Each area reflected a thoughtful approach to student development and wellbeing. What stood out most was the strong sense of community. The passion and collaboration among staff, students, and families have created an inclusive culture where every child is valued and encouraged to reach their full potential. It was heartening to see such a cohesive environment where learning is joyful and meaningful. For me, this visit reinforced how essential strong, compassionate leadership and a supportive school culture are in shaping not just the academic outcomes but also the future wellbeing of our young learners.

tree_branches.name: Birthday Message - Edwin Robertson
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Birthday Message - Edwin Robertson
tree_branches.text: Mr JORDAN LANE ( Ryde ) —I ask the House to join me in wishing Edwin Robertson a joyous 47th birthday! Edwin's wife, Joanne Chua-Robertson, asked me to share these heartfelt words in the Parliament: "Happy Birthday to the Love of my Life! Wishing you, Edwin, the best birthday, many happy returns today and many, many more birthdays to come! We love you! James, Ella and your Tai Tai, Joanne xoxoxoxo." It truly is a wonderful thing to celebrate a birthday with the love and support of those closest to you, and I am humbled to be able to play a small role in making Edwin's day a little extra special. May this birthday be filled with love, laughter, and cherished moments that can be taken forward on life's journey. Wishing you continued happiness and prosperity in the years ahead. Happy birthday Edwin!

tree_branches.name: Mr JORDAN LANE
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Birthday Message - Edwin Robertson > Mr JORDAN LANE
tree_branches.text: Mr JORDAN LANE ( Ryde ) —I rise today to ask the House to join me in recognising and congratulating Melrose Estate Agents for winning the 2025 Northern District Local Business Award in the Outstanding Real Estate Agency category. This being the 3rd win for this business, this is an extraordinary achievement and a well deserved one indeed. Melrose Estate Agents has redefined what it means to be a real estate agency, placing clients and their goals at the heart of everything they do. More than simply facilitating property transactions, they have combined expert knowledge, genuine care, and a fresh, client-first perspective, helping individuals not only navigate the property market but also realise their broader aspirations. Their approach is grounded in building long-lasting relationships and delivering real value at every step. Melrose's success reflects the strength and evolution of Ryde's business community - one that values innovation, trust, and putting people first. Your passion and perseverance have not gone unnoticed.

tree_branches.text: Mr JORDAN LANE ( Ryde ) —I rise today to ask the House to join me in recognising and congratulating Melrose Estate Agents for winning the 2025 Northern District Local Business Award in the Outstanding Real Estate Agency category. This being the 3rd win for this business, this is an extraordinary achievement and a well deserved one indeed. Melrose Estate Agents has redefined what it means to be a real estate agency, placing clients and their goals at the heart of everything they do. More than simply facilitating property transactions, they have combined expert knowledge, genuine care, and a fresh, client-first perspective, helping individuals not only navigate the property market but also realise their broader aspirations. Their approach is grounded in building long-lasting relationships and delivering real value at every step. Melrose's success reflects the strength and evolution of Ryde's business community - one that values innovation, trust, and putting people first. Your passion and perseverance have not gone unnoticed.

tree_branches.name: Birthday - Kangan Sharma
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Birthday - Kangan Sharma
tree_branches.text: Mr JORDAN LANE ( Ryde ) —I ask the House to join me in wishing Kangan Sharma a happy 34th birthday and note the following message for Hansard: "Happiest birthday Kangan." It truly is a wonderful thing to celebrate a birthday in a community like Ryde, and I am humbled to be able to play a small role in making Kangan's day that little bit extra special. As you reflect on your birthday, I hope the memories are filled with love, laughter, and cherished moments that you will take on your journey in the future. Wishing you continued happiness and prosperity in the years ahead. Happy birthday Kangan!

tree_branches.name: Motorcycling for Prostate Cancer
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Motorcycling for Prostate Cancer
tree_branches.text: Mr STEVE WHAN ( Monaro — Minister for Skills, TAFE and Tertiary Education ) —Three members of our community are about to embark on a huge motorcycle journey to raise money for the Prostate Cancer Foundation of Australia. Lloyd Venables, Phil Jamieson, and Paul Duncan from the Snowy Monaro region are riding 4,500 kilometres in one week across the county to Esperance. That's an amazing effort for a great cause. As the most diagnosed cancer, we all know someone (including my uncle, the late Andrew Papworth) who has been affected by prostate cancer. Over 26,000 men are expected to be diagnosed with prostate cancer this year, with close to 4,000 men dying each year in Australia from the disease. I want to thank Lloyd, Phil, and Paul for their fundraising and wish them luck on their ride across the country.

tree_branches.name: Mr STEVE WHAN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Motorcycling for Prostate Cancer > Mr STEVE WHAN
tree_branches.text: Mr STEVE WHAN ( Monaro — Minister for Skills, TAFE and Tertiary Education ) —At the end of this week on Saturday the 18th, Queanbeyan is holding its annual Diwali-Mela lantern festival, and it's set to be the biggest one yet. I've spoken about this festival before, but I believe it's worth reiterating: our diversity is one of our great strengths as a community, and as a country. Coming together to celebrate the triumph of light over dark, and good over evil is a wonderfully fitting way to celebrate this strength. Thanks to a successful grant application, Queanbeyan-Palerang Council were awarded nearly $54,000 to put towards making this festival of light even brighter. I wouldn't dare miss it and I can't wait to see everyone there.

tree_branches.name: Jemmia Luck
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Jemmia Luck
tree_branches.text: Mr PAUL TOOLE ( Bathurst ) —Congratulations to young Bathurst apprentice Jemmia Luck who has taken out a major award at the 2025 Skillset Awards event held at Taronga Western Plains Zoo at Dubbo. Jemmia was named the First Nations Trainee of the Year for her outstanding work with her host employer, Ochre Health in Bathurst. Her dedication to learning, cultural advocacy and community engagement has made her a standout performer amongst her peers. Jemmia's success in her Business Administration traineeship reflects the value of culturally supportive workplaces and the importance of creating pathways for Indigenous youth in healthcare and beyond. Well done Jemmia and best of luck as you forge a career on the back of your success with Skillset.

tree_branches.name: Mr PAUL TOOLE
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Jemmia Luck > Mr PAUL TOOLE
tree_branches.text: Mr PAUL TOOLE ( Bathurst ) —Taking on an apprenticeship has created a wonderful career pathway for Kandos-Rylstone local and proud Wiradjuri man Corey Amstrong-Lane. His outstanding dedication and work ethic has resulted in him being named Skillset's Apprentice of the Year. Corey is completing his Certificate III in Mobile Plant Technology with Yancoal Moolarben Coal Operations Since 2022, he has become a highly skilled and trusted tradesperson, earning multiple high-risk work licences and leading major shutdown projects. His commitment to safety and excellence has earned Moolarben's Values Champions Excellence Award. As well, Corey is also a passionate advocate for vocational training and Indigenous leadership, sharing his story at community events and mentoring young Indigenous students. His journey from Skillset's Young Connect program to Apprenticeship of the Year is a testament to his drive and impact on the workplace. Congratulations Corey, you are indeed a wonderful role model and will hopefully inspire others to follow in your footsteps.

tree_branches.name: Reuben James Ico - Corpus Christi College Maroubra
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Reuben James Ico - Corpus Christi College Maroubra
tree_branches.text: Dr MARJORIE O'NEILL ( Coogee ) —It is a great pleasure to recognise Reuben James Ico for winning The VET Excellence Awards from The Youth Partnership. The award is designed to celebrate the achievements of hardworking students studding in VET. Each school participating in the Youth Partnership program from the Coogee electorate were asked to select one Year 12 VET student to receive an Excellence Award. For Corpus Christi College Maroubra the award went to Reuben James Ico. The winning student is selected based their consistent and high level participating in all class activities. They also must have completed all assessment tasks to an excellent standard, displayed a positive attitude and completed their mandatory work placement. Again, congratulations to Reuben.

tree_branches.name: Bangladeshi Australian Business Expo
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Bangladeshi Australian Business Expo
tree_branches.text: Mr NATHAN HAGARTY ( Leppington ) —Although I wasn't able to attend, I want to acknowledge the tremendous success of this year's Bangladeshi Australian Business Expo, held by the Australian Bangladesh Business Forum at the Sydney Masonic Centre. Bringing together professionals across sectors from textiles and IT to agriculture, education, and food, this Expo created momentum for local businesses and global connections. It wasn't just a showcase of products and services, it was a space for ideas to move, partnerships to form, and cultural pride to shine through. These kinds of events matter. They strengthen our economy, open new doors for trade and investment, and celebrate the rich contributions of Bangladeshi heritage to our community. Congratulations to Abdul Ratan Khan and the entire Forum committee for organising such an impactful event. It's through gatherings like this that we grow stronger together, both in business and in community.

tree_branches.name: Mr NATHAN HAGARTY
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Bangladeshi Australian Business Expo > Mr NATHAN HAGARTY
tree_branches.text: Mr NATHAN HAGARTY ( Le ppington ) —On the 29 of August, I had the pleasure of attending the Southern District Soccer Football Association 80th anniversary. The SDFA aims to develop life-long participants in football by creating inclusive, enjoyable, and aspirational experiences for every player. They strive to ignite passion for the game and build strong, lasting relationships within the football community. Celebrating 80 years is a remarkable achievement, a testament to the enduring spirit and commitment of everyone involved, from players and coaches to volunteers and supporters. I would like to thank President Andy Favalaro, Secretary Gino Marra and the entire committee for always supporting our local athletes. Particularly the clubs in my electorate ‑ Kemps Creek United, Austral, Liverpool City Robins and Leppington Lions. Congratulations on this significant occasion. The associations unwavering support and dedication have created an environment where athletes can thrive. This milestone not only reflects everyone's hard work but also the strength of a community committed to empowering every athlete to perform at their best.

tree_branches.name: Liverpool Art Society Annual Exhibition Launch
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Liverpool Art Society Annual Exhibition Launch
tree_branches.text: Mr NATHAN HAGARTY ( Leppington ) —Though the Liverpool Powerhouse sits just beyond my electorate's borders, I want to take a moment to honour the incredible artistic talent that continues to shine across our region. The 27th Annual Liverpool Art Society Exhibition was a celebration of creativity, hosted throughout September at the Powerhouse. From emerging young artists to seasoned creatives, the exhibition brought together a rich array of works that speak to the depth and diversity of artistic expression in Southwest Sydney. I'd especially like to congratulate the winners of the Mixed Media 2D category, which I was proud to sponsor. Mariam Abbas, Rebecca Anne Brady, and Margaret Tra, each offered moving and thought-provoking pieces that reflect the personal, the cultural, and the universal. Their works remind us that art can hold memory, challenge perception, and offer space for healing. Congratulations to all the exhibitors and entrants. Your work is a testament to the talent, imagination, and resilience of our community. And to the Liverpool Art Society, thank you for making it all possible.
