tree_branches.name: Barbie Bird
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Barbie Bird
tree_branches.text: Ms JENNY AITCHISON ( Maitland — Minister for Regional Transport, and Minister for Roads ) —Congratulations to Barbie Bird, a stalwart of the Maitland District Netball Association. Barbie's efforts have inspired the association to create an award recognising an individual who shares Barbie's values of sportsmanship and positive, supportive contributions to their team. A much-loved member of the Maitland netball community, Barbie has volunteered her time at both club and association level for more than 40 years, longer than anyone else in the club's 78-year history. Barbie was awarded life membership of the association in 1996 and has been awarded the Australian Sports Medal. She has also received several other commendations including the Paul Harris Recognition Citation – Rotary Club of Maitland Sunrise. At the age of 82, Barbie still works hard every week organising stock, supervising helpers, working in the canteen, and socialising with members and their families. Well done Barbie, your hard work is an inspiration to the Maitland community.

tree_branches.name: Ms JENNY AITCHISON
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Barbie Bird > Ms JENNY AITCHISON
tree_branches.text: Ms JENNY AITCHISON ( Maitland — Minister for Regional Transport, and Minister for Roads ) —VALE Judy Nicholson, a pivotal member of the Maitland Historical Society and past Local History Librarian, who passed away suddenly in August. Judy made a huge contribution to several local organisations, including Maitland's Australian Museum of Clothing and Textiles. Members of these organisations recently gathered to remember Judy's tireless work for her community. This includes her role as the editor of the Historical Society's quarterly bulletin. Judy made sure she left a detailed "template", making the job of those who will follow so much easier. Judy was also a valued volunteer with the Friends of Grossman and Brough Houses, where she generously shared her passion for history and community. Before Judy retired and started her volunteering career, she worked in the local history section of Maitland City Council library. She was always extremely helpful in answering questions and providing research material to curious community members. I join the Maitland community in remembering Judy's important contribution and mark her sad passing.

tree_branches.name: Vicki Mendyk - WayAhead Finalist
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Vicki Mendyk - WayAhead Finalist
tree_branches.text: Ms JENNY AITCHISON ( Maitland — Minister for Regional Transport, and Minist er for Roads ) —Congratulations to Maitland local Vicki Mendyk, who was a worthy finalist in the recent WayAhead Mental Health Awards. These awards honour the achievements of individuals and organisations who have championed mental health awareness and support in communities across New South Wales. One of only three individuals selected as a finalist, Vicki was recognised both as the founder and for her ongoing work with UMatter, a local Maitland group dedicated to suicide prevention and awareness. UMatter provides free community support, from training sessions and mid-year check-in dinners to stalls at local events. Together with her partner, Lyndsay Walker, Vicki also leads the 12-hour Suicide Awareness Walk, now in its third year. Vicki also works part-time as a disability care worker, helping to support people through every stage of suicide risk – before, during and after crisis. Vicki, your inspiring work continues to remind us all that every life matters, and that one life lost is one too many.

tree_branches.name: Willoughby Pet Competition 2025
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Willoughby Pet Competition 2025
tree_branches.text: Mr TIM JAMES ( Willoughby ) —The Willoughby Pet Competition 2025 was another wonderful celebration of the animals that bring so much joy and companionship to our lives. Each year this local competition highlights the special bonds between pets and their families, and this year's entries were truly outstanding. Congratulations to our winners. First place went to Pickles, a Rhodesian cross loved by Chris and Juls. After being adopted twice before, Pickles has found her forever home and means the world to her family. Second place went to Indigo the cat, nominated by Ariana and her family. Indigo is playful and affectionate and even donates blood to help other cats in need. Third place went to Bluey the French Bulldog, loved by Leo and his family. Bluey and Leo share a special, heart-warming bond. An honourable mention goes to Pippa the greyhound. A gentle former race dog, Pippa gave endless love and kindness. She has sadly gained her angel wings, and her story was proudly shared by Marleen. Thank you to all entrants and to Rod and Narelle from Pet Town at Westfield Chatswood for sponsoring this community event.

tree_branches.text: Mr TIM JAMES ( Willoughby ) —Ms Unity Taylor-Hill has made an outstanding contribution to public education through a decade of leadership at Anzac Park Public School in Cammeray. As the school's inaugural principal, appointed when Anzac Park PS was established in 2015, she has shaped its vision, culture and identity from day one. Under her leadership, Anzac Park has grown into a thriving, innovative and highly regarded public school, known for its strong community spirit, modern approach to learning and commitment to student success. Ms Taylor-Hill guided the school through its formative years, overseeing enrolment growth, developing contemporary teaching practices, and fostering an inclusive and collaborative school community. After ten years of dedicated service, Ms Taylor-Hill has now been promoted to the role of Leader – Primary Curriculum within the NSW Department of Education. This is a well-deserved recognition of her expertise and leadership. The Anzac Park Public School community deeply thanks Ms Taylor-Hill for her years of service and wishes her every success in this important new role supporting schools across the state.

tree_branches.name: Dr Mackenzie Little
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Dr Mackenzie Little
tree_branches.text: Mr TIM JAMES ( Willoughby ) —Dr Mackenzie Little has again done us proud, claiming bronze in the women's javelin at the World Athletics Championships in Tokyo. Remarkably, this world-class performance came just days after completing multiple night shifts as a young doctor at Royal North Shore Hospital. Arriving in Tokyo after saving a man from a heart attack, Mackenzie threw an incredible 65.54 metres in qualifying, the longest throw of the event, before securing bronze in the final with 63.58 metres. This result matches her bronze from Budapest and follows her Paris Olympics campaign. Her achievement is even more extraordinary given the demands of her medical residency. Mackenzie used annual leave to compete, working emergency shifts right up to her departure. Her ability to excel in both elite sport and medicine is inspiring and reflects immense resilience, dedication and talent. Mackenzie is a shining example of Australian excellence, balancing service to the community with representing our nation on the world stage. Her achievements are a source of immense pride for Royal North Shore Hospital and the Willoughby community.

tree_branches.name: Active Living OT
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Active Living OT
tree_branches.text: Mr PAUL TOOLE ( Bathurst ) —Making a difference to the quality of life for their clients has led to much deserved recognition for everyone involve with the success story that is Active Living OT. The business has triumphed to take out first place in the category for "Outstanding New Business" at the recent Oberon Business and Tourist Association Awards. Based in Oberon, Active Living OT is a mobile occupational therapy service which takes pride in proudly supporting individuals and families across the Central West of New South Wales. Established in 2024, Active Living OT excels in being able to deliver personalised therapy in the comfort of clients' homes, schools and workplaces – meeting people where they live and thrive. With a strong focus on functional independence , neurodiversity-affirming practice and holistic support, the business works with children, teenagers and adults to building meaningful skills and confidence which is reflected in this award from the local community. Active Living OT is clearly passionate about creating lasting change in rural communities through accessible, compassionate, and evidence-based care tailored to each client's unique needs and goals. Congratulations to everyone involved with making Active Living OT the success story that is in the making.

tree_branches.name: Mr PAUL TOOLE
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Active Living OT > Mr PAUL TOOLE
tree_branches.text: Mr PAUL TOOLE ( Bathurst ) —Taking on an apprenticeship has created a wonderful career pathway for Kandos-Rylstone local and proud Wiradjuri man Corey Amstrong-Lane. His outstanding dedication and work ethic has resulted in him being named Skillset's Apprentice of the Year. Corey is completing his Certificate III in Mobile Plant Technology with Yancoal Moolarben Coal Operations Since 2022, he has become a highly skilled and trusted tradesperson, earning multiple high-risk work licences and leading major shutdown projects. His commitment to safety and excellence has earned Moolarben's Values Champions Excellence Award. As well, Corey is also a passionate advocate for vocational training and Indigenous leadership, sharing his story at community events and mentoring young Indigenous students. His journey from Skillset's Young Connect program to Apprenticeship of the Year is a testament to his drive and impact on the workplace. Congratulations Corey, you are indeed a wonderful role model and will hopefully inspire others to follow in your footsteps.

tree_branches.name: Sonder Youth
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Sonder Youth
tree_branches.text: Ms LIZA BUTLER ( South Coast ) —I would like to acknowledge Sonder Youth, a youth-led charity founded in 2017 on the NSW South Coast, for its inspiring work empowering young people aged 14 to 18 to lead community-driven change. Sonder delivers mental health and leadership programs that build confidence, resilience, and wellbeing across regional communities through strong partnerships with local services and schools. Its flagship initiatives - the Changemakers Program and South Coast Changemakers Forum - equips young people with practical leadership skills, mental health strategies, and opportunities to deliver real social impact projects. In 2024, Sonder expanded its reach to the Southern Highlands, Riverina Murray, and Hunter New England, partnering with organisations such as Headspace Nowra and Cessnock City Council to deliver tailored youth development programs. I am delighted that $25,000 in one-off funding has been provided to support Sonder Youth's 2025 Changemakers Camp on the NSW South Coast. This peer-led program brought together 50 young people to build mental health resilience, leadership, and community connection nurturing the next generation of regional leaders.

tree_branches.name: Ms LIZA BUTLER
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Sonder Youth > Ms LIZA BUTLER
tree_branches.text: Ms LIZA BUTLER ( South Co ast ) —It was a true joy to celebrate Lyrebird Preschool's remarkable milestone - 50 years of nurturing, educating, and inspiring young minds in East Nowra. For half a century, Lyrebird Preschool has been a cornerstone of our community, giving generations of children the best possible start in life through quality early childhood education. This success story began under the leadership of Founding Director, Lola Wilson, whose 25 years of dedication set the standards of excellence that remain today. Lola's vision shaped the preschool's philosophy, from creating the first garden from bare ground to building deep and enduring connections with our local Aboriginal community. The celebration brought together past and present families at the pre-school for a wonderful gathering filled with joy, laughter, and fond memories. It was a heartwarming reflection of just how loved and valued this pre-school is within our community. Director Sharon O'Brien and her passionate team continue this proud legacy by fostering inclusion, creativity, and community spirit for every child and family who walks through their doors. Congratulations to everyone past and present on 50 wonderful years, and here's to the next 50 of learning, laughter, and belonging.

tree_branches.name: Manyana Rural Fire Service Brigade
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Manyana Rural Fire Service Brigade
tree_branches.text: Ms LIZA BUTLER ( South Coast ) —I would like to recognise and congratulate the Manyana Rural Fire Service Brigade on the official opening of their new $3.48 million fire station, unveiled on Sunday, 28 September. Located on Bendalong Road, this impressive new facility replaces the old Cunjarong Point shed and now provides a modern, central base for volunteers serving Manyana, Bendalong, and the wider Shoalhaven region. With four truck bays, a multifunction room, kitchen, office, locker rooms, and a breathing apparatus room, the station has been purpose-built to meet the growing needs of our local community. The brigade's 43 dedicated members have demonstrated remarkable courage and commitment, particularly during and after the Black Summer bushfires. This new station stands as a testament to their resilience and the community's deep gratitude for their ongoing service and protection. Congratulations to the Manyana RFS Brigade and everyone involved in bringing this important project to life - it is a well-deserved investment in our volunteers and the safety and strength of our South Coast communities.

tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Walcha CWA
tree_branches.text: Mr BRENDA N MOYLAN ( Northern Tablelands ) —I recognise the achievements of the Walcha branch of the Country Women's Association (CWA) on their 100-year milestone! The group was formed by women living in remote and isolated areas to improve health. Today the CWA is the largest women's organisation in Australia lobbying for change, helping the local community and creating a network of support for the cause. I congratulate past and present members for their tireless efforts over the last 100 years, with special mention of Patroness Gwen Lisle, who has been a supporting member for 43 years and life member Fay Hawkins, who has been an active member for 33 years. Thank you to the current committee members, including: Vicki McIvor, Di Bazeley, Anne Young, Helen Tisdell, Lynne Schmidt, Samantha Bayley, Ann Levingston and Helen Wauch. Throughout the year the group has cooking and craft days, hold street stalls and caters for events, raising funds and awareness around supports provided. I commend all those involved, for their hard work, selflessly giving of their time to improve the lives of others. Organisations such as the CWA in regional towns, benefit greatly from the ongoing support and commitment such volunteers give. Well done on this wonderful milestone!

tree_branches.name: Mr BRENDAN MOYLAN
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Walcha CWA > Mr BRENDAN MOYLAN
tree_branches.text: Mr BRENDAN MOYLAN ( Northern Tablelands ) —I recognise the many achievements of Inverell local Josh Cathie. Josh is an extraordinary young leader, whose achievements speak volumes about his integrity, drive and generosity. His leadership, initiative and dedication have made him a standout figure in the Inverell Shire and beyond. I congratulate Josh on his prestigious Minister's Award for Excellence in Student Achievement. Josh has been a vital member of the Inverell Youth Advisory Council for the past 3 years and was Chair for the last 12 months. Beyond this work, Josh is a committed member of the Inverell Toastmasters and has excelled in public speaking competitions. Honing his communication skills has allowed Josh to organise several charity events, which are reflective of his compassionate nature. Josh also serves as a corporal in the Australian Air Force Cadets, demonstrating his leadership skills, discipline, responsibility and a strong sense of service. I commend Josh on his achievements and the role model he presents for the youth in the region, and he is a shining example of what can be accomplished through hard work and dedication.

tree_branches.name: Mungindi Cotton Growers Association
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Mungindi Cotton Growers Association
tree_branches.text: Mr BRENDAN MOYLAN ( Northern Tablelands ) —I recognise the Mungindi Cotton Growers Association on staging a very successful 9-hole Ambrose Charity Golf Day, an annual initiative raising vital funds to support local schools, medical and aged services, churches and sporting clubs. The day raised an impressive $30,000 and will be donated to 19 groups. Over the past five years alone, this event has raised a phenomenal $120,000 with the sole purpose of giving back to the Mungindi community. I congratulate all involved in organising the golf day, including the current hard-working committee members, including: President Ben Warby, Treasurer Rebecca Longworth and Secretary Ashlee Johnston, along with members Nellie Lawson, Mick Freeman and Sam Heagney. Special thanks to the 45 generous sponsors, 140 players, the Mungindi Community Preschool and Daycare for catering, volunteers for providing roaming drink carts, along with the Mungindi Golf Club members, who turned out an exceptional course for the day. I commend all involved, for working tirelessly behind the scenes ensuring the Ambrose came together without a hitch. This is what's special about country people in country towns - they know how to pull together, make it happen, whilst taking the opportunity to give back to their own.

tree_branches.name: Mosman Art Prize 2025
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Mosman Art Prize 2025
tree_branches.text: Ms FELICITY WILSON ( North Shore ) —I extend my heartfelt congratulations to the team at the Mosman Art Gallery for organising another successful art prize competition in 2025. The brilliant Mosman Art Prize is now in its 78th year and is Australia's longest-running municipal art award. It is widely regarded as the most respected and relevant painting prize in the country. The winner of the prize for 2025 is Indigenous Painter Mark Maurangi Carrol for his work blue boat (crowd on the island of Mangaia). In Mark's own words, the painting "Reimagines a 1900 photograph taken by Frederick W. Sears on the island of Mangaia, where a crowd observes the government vessel Tutanaekai." Five further art awards - in addition to the acquisitive major prize won by Mark - were also awarded as part of the competition. This year, the art prize received over 1,400 entries from across the country, with 72 finalists featuring in the exhibition. The scope of entries shows the prestige attached to the Mosman Art Gallery and its annual art prize and this is due to the hard work of Steven Alderton, Kelly McDonald and the rest of the gallery's staff.

tree_branches.name: Ms FELICITY WILSON
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Mosman Art Prize 2025 > Ms FELICITY WILSON
tree_branches.text: Ms FELICITY WILSON ( North Shore ) —Congratulations to Middle Harbour Yacht Club as the start of the sailing season begins. With a membership of over 900, Middle Harbour Yacht Club is one of Australia's largest yacht clubs and recognised as a national leader in sail training and associated education. Supporting the entire spectrum of sailing through from the Australian Olympic Team to Sydney to Hobart racers, cruising yachts, to Sailability and learning to sail, Middle Harbour Yacht Club is a true community club. It was an extra-special start to the season with the club launching a new start boat which I helped name Legacy after providing funding support, supplemented by charitable and member donations. Legacy replaced the long-serving Hugh George. Legacy was christened in a special sea-sailing ceremony, and it was a privilege to join yacht club officials to celebrate the new vessel. Well done to club Commodore Rob Aldis, along with Chief Executive Andrew Forbes, on securing Legacy and for hosting this special season opening.

tree_branches.name: New Season Starts for Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > New Season Starts for Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron
tree_branches.text: Ms FELICITY WILSON ( North Shore ) —Many congratulations to the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron on the start of the new sailing season, which began on Sunday 14 September. The Kirribilli-based Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron is one of the country's most well-known yacht clubs and offers world class facilities for sailors and non-sailors alike. Everyone in our community is very proud of the club's rich sailing history, including leading the first three Australian challenges for the America's Cup. The club's season was launched with the Commodore's address followed by the commencement of the Parade of Sail. I'm pleased for Club Commodore Russell Taylor and his members for such a successful start to the season. I was very happy to be in attendance for the launch and see so many impressive vessels with crews ready and eager to compete. I was also glad to see so many youngsters at the launch. I'm confident these budding sailors will be the future of the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron.

tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > New Season Starts for Middle Harbour Yacht Club > Ms FELICITY WILSON
tree_branches.text: Ms FELICITY WILSON ( North Shore ) —Congratulations to Middle Harbour Yacht Club as the start of the sailing season begins. With a membership of over 900, Middle Harbour Yacht Club is one of Australia's largest yacht clubs and recognised as a national leader in sail training and associated education. Supporting the entire spectrum of sailing through from the Australian Olympic Team to Sydney to Hobart racers, cruising yachts, to Sailability and learning to sail, Middle Harbour Yacht Club is a true community club. It was an extra-special start to the season with the club launching a new start boat which I helped name Legacy after providing funding support, supplemented by charitable and member donations. Legacy replaced the long-serving Hugh George. Legacy was christened in a special sea-sailing ceremony, and it was a privilege to join yacht club officials to celebrate the new vessel. Well done to club Commodore Rob Aldis, along with Chief Executive Andrew Forbes, on securing Legacy and for hosting this special season opening.

tree_branches.name: Laura Barnett
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Laura Barnett
tree_branches.text: Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP ( Newcastle ) —The beach has always been an important part of Newcastle, and so too has education around beach safety. Dixon Park Surf Life Saving Club's Laura Barnett has been recognised as the NSW Surf Lif Saving Trainer of the Year, at the NSW Awards of Excellence ceremony. The ceremony focuses on recognising volunteer lifesavers and their supporters in their ongoing efforts to keep our beaches safe. Laura has been recognised for her significant impact with Dixon Park, for her work in education and training through programs such as their annual skills training, maintenance practicals and bronze medallion courses. Great job Laura, I thank you for your continued commitment to the safety of beachgoers in our region.

tree_branches.name: Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Laura Barnett > Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP
tree_branches.text: Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP ( Newcastle ) —I want to congratulate Phoenix Denny on his recent competition in the 2025 World Scholars Global Round in Thailand. Pheonix is a year 6 student at St Joseph's Primary School Merewether. He is the first High Potential and Gifted Education student to represent the Maitland‑Newcastle Catholic Diocese at an international competition. The World Scholars Cup was established as an alternative to traditional academic competitions, with small teams competing in challenges, multiple choice tests, debate and collaborative writing. Phoenix's passion and skill for debating saw him shine at the regional round and allowing him to advance to the global round. I want to congratulate Phoenix on his incredible efforts, and look forward to seeing what he accomplishes in the future.

tree_branches.name: Doc's Megasave Chemist
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Doc's Megasave Chemist
tree_branches.text: Mr TIM CRAKANTHORP ( Newcastle ) —Docs Megasave Chemist in Marketown has earned major recognition after being named Business of the Year at the 2025 Hunter Local Business Awards. More than just a chemist, Docs has proudly served Newcastle for over two decades, known for their late-night service, expert service and excellent prices. They have grown beyond just a place to dispense medicines into a healthcare destination with compounding services and an in-house nurse practitioner. The team has also been involved in numerous local sporting clubs and charities, such as RU Ok Day and Breastfeeding Week. Local businesses are an important part of the Newcastle community, and so too is recognising them. As well as Business of the Year, Docs also took home the Outstanding Pharmacy Award. Congrats to the team of Docs Megasave Pharmacy on their win! You're an asset to the Newcastle community.

tree_branches.name: Dr Chandrika Subramaniyan
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Dr Chandrika Subramaniyan
tree_branches.text: Dr HUGH McDERMOTT ( Prospect ) —On Saturday 27th September, I was delighted to launch Glimpses of Kambaramayanam by Dr Chandrika Subramaniyan, alongside Tamil-language books Siddha Marabu by Vijay Singh and Vidiyal Geethangal by Aru Kumaraselvam. Dr. Chandrika Subramaniyan is a lawyer, community leader and accomplished writer in English and Tamil. Her latest book, Glimpses of Kambaramayanam presents 108 carefully selected verses from the Ramavataram, a 12th-century Tamil epic, accompanied by English translation, transliteration, and meanings in both Tamil and English, especially aimed at enlightening Tamil youth. Vijay Singh, a non-Tamil scholar who mastered the Tamil language, explores profound philosophies of the Siddhars in Siddhar Marabu, (Siddha Traditions). Rooted in ancient Tamil spiritual heritage, these mystical sages are revered for their extraordinary mastery in alchemy, medicine, yoga, and cosmic wisdom, continuing to inspire and guide. Aru Kumaraselvam's Tamil poetry collection Vidiyal Geethangal, (Songs at Dawn) offers reflections and moral insights for daily life. These verses guide and inspire the next generation of our Tamil-Australian community, nurturing cultural pride and personal growth through poetry. Congratulations on this significant achievement and great event. Thank you for your dedicated, and continued service to our proud Tamil community in Prospect Electorate and across Western Sydney.

tree_branches.name: Dr HUGH McDERMOTT
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Dr Chandrika Subramaniyan > Dr HUGH McDERMOTT
tree_branches.text: Dr HUGH McDERMOTT ( Prospect ) —On Sunday 28th September, I was delighted to meet with volunteers and parishioners from Wentworthville Anglican Church and present them with a Community Building Partnership grant. Established more than a century ago in 1919, Wenty Anglican is an historic faith-based community located in the heart of our local Prospect Electorate. Today, the Church conducts English and Tamil language church services on Sundays and operate numerous community-focused services, including language classes for new migrants. Their community garden caters especially to refugees with a history of trauma and marginalised individuals from culturally diverse and disadvantaged backgrounds. This year, Wenty Anglican successfully applied for a Community Building Partnership grant of $42,562 to supply and install reverse cycle air conditioning units for their main auditorium. This grant will ensure that parishioners attending church services and community functions can operate comfortably through the colder and the warmer months. On the day, I joined the Wenty Anglican family during their Sunday service, to pray together and to connect afterwards for morning tea. Thank you David Misztal, Pastor, and all parishioners and volunteers at Wentworthville Anglican Church for your continued service and amazing community spirit.

tree_branches.name: Our Lady Queen of Peace Primary Greystanes
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Our Lady Queen of Peace Primary Greystanes
tree_branches.text: Dr HUGH McDERMOTT ( Pro spect ) —On Thursday 25th September, I was delighted to meet with student leaders and senior staff from Our Lady Queen of Peace Primary Greystanes, to present them a Prospect Electorate Community Building Partnership Grant. Established in 1957, OLQP Primary Greystanes is a wonderful local school committed to learning, community and faith in the heart of Prospect Electorate. Today, the school is a vibrant K-6 learning community with more than 800 students from all walks of life. I was delighted to present OLQP Primary Greystanes with a Grant of $60,000 for an all-new shade structure over their playground and recreational space. This vital funding ensures a safer and more comfortable space for our local school children to play and learn. I was joined on the day by Fr Paul Roberts, Parish Priest, Kym Romanous, Assistant Principal and Year 6 Student Leaders for the Grant presentation. Congratulations Anthony McElhone, Principal and all the teachers and students at OLQP Primary Greystanes on this wonderful upgrade. Thank you for your wonderful community spirit. May the school's patron, Our Lady Queen of Peace guide you in faith and kindness as you continue on your journey of learning.

tree_branches.name: Abbotsford Rowing Club
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Abbotsford Rowing Club
tree_branches.text: Ms STEPHANIE DI PASQUA ( Drummoyne ) —I rise to acknowledge a beloved local sporting club, Abbotsford Rowing Club Since their establishment in 1910 as a women-only club, Abbotsford Rowing Club has grown into a tight knit community of enthusiastic rowers. Over the years, they have supported a number of local school's rowing programs, sharing their passion for the sport with the younger generation. I sincerely congratulate Abbotsford Rowing Club on its successful 2025 Community Building Partnership grant application. The Club was successful in receiving $20,000 for the purchase of a new ute to tow boats to and from regattas. It was my pleasure to meet with the Club members to announce this funding and discuss the importance of this new vehicle. I acknowledge club President Catherine Naito, Vice-President Sue Carew, Secretary Bronwyn Gow and all members of the Management Committee. I also acknowledge Margaret McKenzie who played a vital role in supporting the Club's Community Building Partnership grant application. I thank each of them for their exceptional leadership and dedication to supporting local sport. Congratulations to Abbotsford Rowing Club. I wish all members the very best.

tree_branches.name: Ms STEPHANIE DI PASQUA
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Abbotsford Rowing Club > Ms STEPHANIE DI PASQUA
tree_branches.text: Ms STEPHANIE DI PASQUA ( Drummoyne ) —I rise to sincerely congratulate Olivia O'Keefe from All Hallows Catholic Primary School, Five Dock. Olivia is the proud winner of my 2025 Ferragosto Colouring-In Competition. Olivia's beautiful artwork showed creativity and outstanding attention to detail. Her entry stood out for her vibrant use of colour and ability to capture the spirit of Italy and Ferragosto. It was so evident that she put great thought and care into her entry. I recently had the pleasure of meeting Olivia and her mother Linda to personally congratulate her on her wonderful artwork. They shared that Olivia had dedicated countless hours perfecting her entry, working carefully on every detail to make sure it was perfect. She has a passion for art, and I know her family are immensely proud of her. I would like to sincerely congratulate to Olivia on her outstanding artwork for the 2025 Ferragosto Colouring-in Competition. I look forward to seeing her creativity continue to flourish in the years ahead. I wish her and her family all the very best.

tree_branches.name: Virginia de Luca
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Virginia de Luca
tree_branches.text: Ms STEPHANIE DI PASQ UA ( Drummoyne ) —I rise to sincerely congratulate Virginia De Luca on the release of her children's storybook entitled 'Sweet Legacy – A Story About Nonno'. Sweet Legacy – A Story About Nonno shares the story of Virginia's grandfather Salvatore and father Luigi as they migrated from Italy to Australia and became renowned for their gelato. Through their courage, hard work and passion for hospitality, they built a family legacy that continues to this day. The book is written in both English and Italian, allowing readers of all ages and backgrounds to connect with the story. This bilingual format celebrates the richness of the Italian language and culture whilst helping younger generations preserve their heritage. By sharing the story in both languages, Virginia has created a special story that honours the experience of migrants such as the De Luca family and celebrates the multicultural spirit of our community. Congratulations Virigina on this wonderful achievement. Sweet Legacy - A Story About Nonno is a wonderful book. I wish her all the very best.

tree_branches.name: St George Saints Youth League Men's Basketball Team
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > St George Saints Youth League Men's Basketball Team
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK COURE ( Oatley ) —Speaker, I rise to recognise the outstanding efforts of the St George Saints Youth League Men's basketball team, who recently made it into the semi-finals. Throughout the Waratah League season, the Saints have continued to proudly represent the St George community both on and off the court. In their recent semi-final against the Newcastle Falcons, the team performed exceptionally well. While the final score was not in their favour, each and every player should be proud of their performance on the court. Grassroots sport is so important in our local community and the Saints have continued to exemplify this over many years. Their success is measured not just in wins, but also their sportsmanship and teamwork. I would like to congratulate Coach Luther Shannon, Peter Kospetas, Metheo (Shay Semausu, Tao Smith, Maper Maker Makur, Dylan Akosah, Abdula Hamid Banse, Angelo Tsitos (Assistant Coach), Edward Smith (Assistant Coach), James Wang, Luis Nunez, Mason Nichols, Jaxon Jon Frintzilas, Taine Vilo, Jay Hadman and Kupa Teao on their hard work this season. On behalf of our community, I congratulate the St George Saints and wish them every success in the future.

tree_branches.name: Mr MARK COURE
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > St George Saints Youth League Men's Basketball Team > Mr MARK COURE
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK COURE ( Oatley ) —Speaker, I rise to recognise the outstanding contribution of the volunteers and staff of the Chinese Australian Services Society (CASS), who continue to make an enormous difference in the lives of so many people across our community. I recently had the opportunity to attend their Volunteer Thanksgiving Luncheon, which gave me and members of the community the chance to say thank you for all their hard work. CASS is an organisation that truly embodies the spirit of service. With more than 800 staff members and 450 active volunteers, they provide support to over 8,500 families every single day. Volunteering is one of the cornerstones of Australian life. It reflects our shared belief that no one should ever be left behind and that by helping one another, we strengthen our community. CASS plays a particularly important role in providing culturally appropriate aged care and support, ensuring that people from multicultural and multifaith backgrounds receive care that respects their heritage. I especially acknowledge Professor Stephen Li, Henry Pan and the entire CASS team for their leadership and commitment. I look forward to continuing to work with CASS into the future.

tree_branches.name: Rachel Wu
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Rachel Wu
tree_branches.text: Mr MARK COURE ( Oatley ) —Speaker, I rise to acknowledge Rachel Wu of Georges River College Oatley, who was recently presented with a VET Excellence Award in Hospitality, hosted by The Youth Partnership. The VET Excellence Awards are an annual celebration of the achievements of students undertaking Vocational Education and Training as part of their Higher School Certificate. Students are nominated by their schools, with each award representing months of hard work and discipline. Each September, the event is held at the NSW Parliament, giving recognition to students who excel not only in their coursework but also in their commitment to industry standards and their performance during work placements. Rachel's success in the field of Hospitality reflects an ability to bridge classroom learning with practical application. She has demonstrated a genuine passion for her chosen area of study. These are qualities that will serve her well in her education and in any career she chooses to pursue. I congratulate Rachel on this impressive achievement and commend Georges River College Oatley for supporting their students. Our community is proud of Rachel's accomplishment and I wish her every success in the future.

tree_branches.name: Surfboat Brewery
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Surfboat Brewery
tree_branches.text: Ms JACQUI SCRUBY ( Pittwater ) —Surfboat Brewery in Warriewood is a wonderful example of local creativity, resilience and community spirit thriving on the Northern Beaches. The brewery was opened in August 2024 by Kim Hall and Terri Revell, members of the Northern Beaches Jive social dancing group. Surfboat Brewery grew from a shared love of music, movement and community connection. When their local RSL closed, Kim and Terri found a new way to bring people together — through great craft beer, delicious food, live music, and a welcoming space for locals of all ages. In their very first year, Surfboat Brewery entered the Sydney Royal Beer & Cider Show, Australia's premier beer competition — and came home with medals for all three of their entries: a Gold Medal for Sweeps Stout, and Bronze Medals for Hard to Porter and Hazy Hef. Beyond the awards, Surfboat Brewery has become a true community hub. They host live music, jive, tango, salsa and tap-dancing classes all while providing family-friendly fun every week. Congratulations to Kim, Terri and head brewer Kobey, whose passion and hard work have created a place that brings people together and celebrates the best of Warriewood.

tree_branches.name: Ms JACQUI SCRUBY
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Surfboat Brewery > Ms JACQUI SCRUBY
tree_branches.text: Ms JACQUI SCRUBY ( Pittwater ) —On the 28th of June, Bilgola Plateau Public School celebrated 60 years of high quality education. The school was founded in 1965 when 2 teachers and 25 students first walked up from Avalon Public School to begin their classes. On the 60th anniversary, around 200 students, staff, and community members retraced these historic steps in a special Anniversary Walk. The occasion was made profoundly special by the presence of four original students from that first day. Following the walk, guests enjoyed a complimentary Birthday Afternoon Tea and visited the new School Museum which was curated by the P&C. Principal Cindy Gardiner commended the walkers and shared impressive statistics from the school's 12,000 days, including educating over 3,600 students. The celebration was a moving tribute to the school's rich history, cherished memories and strong community spirit, honouring its journey from a small infants school to the thriving primary school it has developed into. Thank you to all who have contributed to this beautiful school over the past 60 years, including Cindy Gardiner who has been principal for over 10 years. Here's to another 60 wonderful years!

tree_branches.name: Marvin Smith
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Marvin Smith
tree_branches.text: Ms JACQUI SCRUBY ( Pittwater ) —I'd like to recognise Marvin Smith, a 26-year-old Newport local and paramedic whose dedication to helping others reflects the best of our Northern Beaches community. Marvin grew up on the Beaches and first discovered his passion for service through Surf Life Saving and St John Ambulance. That early experience inspired him to pursue a career as a paramedic — a role he carries out every day with compassion, professionalism, and calm under pressure. What makes Marvin truly special is what he gives back outside his working hours. In his own time, he runs voluntary sessions for trainee paramedics, designing realistic, high-pressure scenarios to help them build confidence and clinical skill. His philosophy is simple: "When you share knowledge, you make your colleagues better, the community safer, and the service stronger." Marvin's outstanding contribution to mentoring and emergency care has now been formally recognised — he has been recently acknowledged with a NSW Ambulance Appreciation Award for going above and beyond in saving lives across our state. On behalf of the Pittwater community, I thank Marvin for his leadership, generosity, and extraordinary commitment to others. He is an inspiration to us all.

tree_branches.name: Ms JACQUI SCRUBY
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Marvin Smith > Ms JACQUI SCRUBY
tree_branches.text: Ms JACQUI SCRUBY ( Pittwater ) —On the 28th of June, Bilgola Plateau Public School celebrated 60 years of high quality education. The school was founded in 1965 when 2 teachers and 25 students first walked up from Avalon Public School to begin their classes. On the 60th anniversary, around 200 students, staff, and community members retraced these historic steps in a special Anniversary Walk. The occasion was made profoundly special by the presence of four original students from that first day. Following the walk, guests enjoyed a complimentary Birthday Afternoon Tea and visited the new School Museum which was curated by the P&C. Principal Cindy Gardiner commended the walkers and shared impressive statistics from the school's 12,000 days, including educating over 3,600 students. The celebration was a moving tribute to the school's rich history, cherished memories and strong community spirit, honouring its journey from a small infants school to the thriving primary school it has developed into. Thank you to all who have contributed to this beautiful school over the past 60 years, including Cindy Gardiner who has been principal for over 10 years. Here's to another 60 wonderful years!

tree_branches.name: Picnic for Peace
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Picnic for Peace
tree_branches.text: Ms DONNA DAVIS ( Parramatta ) —I am pleased to recognise a powerful and timely initiative - Sydney's first Picnic for Peace, held on Sunday 31 August at Wentworth Common Oval, Sydney Olympic Park. Organised by the Justice and Peace Office of the Archdiocese of Sydney, led by Fr Peter Smith, the event brought together around 150 people from across faiths, cultures and generations to stand together for peace, unity, strength and hope in challenging times. In a world where division and mistrust often dominate headlines, this interfaith and intercultural gathering was a simple yet powerful reminder of what binds us. Through shared food, music, storytelling and heartfelt conversations, Picnic for Peace created a space where people could connect beyond difference and reclaim common ground. As Fr Peter beautifully said - "Part of the dream is to stop the 'othering' of people, to stop this divide between 'us' and 'them." The event marked the launch of a broader movement, with ongoing monthly peace walks, webinars and table talks planned in the months ahead. Congratulations to all involved for creating a space of joy, reflection and solidarity. It is community-led actions like this that restore hope and inspire real, lasting peace.

tree_branches.text: Ms DONNA DAVIS ( Parramatta ) —It was an honour to join in the sesquicentenary celebrations of Arthur Phillip High School on 26 August. Since 1875, Arthur Phillip High has been a cornerstone of our community, nurturing generations of students both in academics, the arts and sport. Arthur Phillip High is not just about learning; it is about preparing students for life. It was a pleasure to meet several former students some who meetup with their fellow alumni– even some who were students during its Centenary celebrations. Arthur Phillip High School was originally part of the Parramatta Public South School renamed Parramatta in 1907. In 1960 the secondary classes were established as Arthur Phillip HS In 2020 the school moved into a new eleven storey high rise building on Macquarie Street. One of the standout characteristics of Arthur Phillip is the diversity of its students and staff. It enriches their perspectives and heightens their appreciation of the cultures, languages and faiths reflected in our community. To mark 150 years, the school published a cookbook that highlights the rich and diverse school community. Congratulations Arthur Phillips High School on this significant milestone. Here's to another 150 years of learning and thriving together!

tree_branches.name: Regency Day Out
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Regency Day Out
tree_branches.text: Ms DONNA DAVIS ( Parramatta ) —Congratulations to the National Trust (NSW Branch) on the success of the Regency Day Out at Old Government House, a truly delightful event that combined history and culture in a fun-filled atmosphere while bringing our community closer together. The Regency Day Out was a fantastic opportunity for people of all ages to step back in time, explore the elegance of the Regency era and enjoy a unique blend of historical talks, a picturesque picnic, dancing around the maypole and vibrant vintage markets. The event perfectly captured the spirit of the Regency Era that is a popular time in history due to the writings of Jane Austen and her contemporaries. The grounds of Old Government House was the perfect setting to admire period fashion, browse through vintage treasures or enjoy a relaxing picnic in the beautiful surroundings. It was a day filled with vintage cosplay and connection to a bygone era that shaped Parramatta and continues to be a tourist drawcard. Thank you to the National Trust for creating such a memorable and enjoyable experience I look forward to events like this becoming a staple on the local calendar to showcase our incredible heritage sites and characters.

tree_branches.name: St Patrick's School Tournament of the Minds
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > St Patrick's School Tournament of the Minds
tree_branches.text: Mr STEVE WHAN ( Monaro — Minister for Skills, TAFE and Tertiary Education ) —Congratulations to students at St Patrick's Parish School in Cooma for their impressive display and success in the Tournament of the Minds, a critical thinking and problem-solving competition for primary and secondary aged students. Two of the three St Pats teams have made it to the finals in the Arts Secondary, and STEM Secondary categories, with the third team placing second in Social Science Secondary and receiving an Honours recognition. The six schools from the ACT and surrounding regions who've made it to finals will be competing against schools from all over the country as well as internationally. St Pats is the only school in the Monaro region to have two teams make it to the finals. Congratulations to the students and their teachers for this wonderful achievement, and good luck in the finals!

tree_branches.text: Mr STEVE WHAN ( Monaro — Minister for Skills, TAFE and Tertiary Education ) —At the end of this week on Saturday the 18th, Queanbeyan is holding its annual Diwali-Mela lantern festival, and it's set to be the biggest one yet. I've spoken about this festival before, but I believe it's worth reiterating: our diversity is one of our great strengths as a community, and as a country. Coming together to celebrate the triumph of light over dark, and good over evil is a wonderfully fitting way to celebrate this strength. Thanks to a successful grant application, Queanbeyan-Palerang Council were awarded nearly $54,000 to put towards making this festival of light even brighter. I wouldn't dare miss it and I can't wait to see everyone there.

tree_branches.name: Trilogy Foundation Christmas In July
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Trilogy Foundation Christmas In July
tree_branches.text: Ms KYLIE WILKINSON ( East Hills ) —I congratulate the Trilogy Foundation Canterbury Bankstown on the success of its Christmas in July event this year, which raised an impressive $15,354 to advance education for children with special needs in our community. Hosted for the third year in a row by Padstow Bowling and Snooker Club, the event brought together local supporters to raise funds for vital educational initiatives. With this year's proceeds, the Foundation has already funded a submission from Koorana Preschool for new sensory equipment at its Bass Hill site, where 20% of enrolments are children with additional needs. Support has also been extended to Revesby Public School's 10-day Swimming and Water Safety Program, designed to make swimming accessible for students in the support unit. The Trilogy Foundation continues to make a meaningful difference by identifying and supporting all abilities programs across education, sport, and recreation. I thank Maureen, Glen, Bob, Pauline, Angela, Kirrily and the entire Trilogy Foundation team for their dedication to ensuring every child in our community has the opportunity to learn, participate and thrive.

tree_branches.text: Ms KYLIE WILKINSON ( East Hills ) —Congratulations to the Bankstown Bruins coaches and managers who have been recognised with awards this year. Special recognition goes to Cooper Avery for receiving the Coaching Recognition Award, to Spiro Stamatatos and Lauryn Curtin for being named Robbie Cadee Coaches of the Year, and to Kate Filemu for her excellent work as manager. These honours reflect your outstanding leadership, commitment, and the vital role you play in the success of the team. I also want to congratulate the Bankstown Bruins on an impressive season. Your dedication, teamwork, and perseverance have truly paid off, and it's inspiring to see local talent performing at such a high level on the basketball court. The Bruins are an important part of our East Hills community. By bringing people together from all backgrounds, you've built a strong sense of unity and pride that extends beyond the game. Thank you to the players, coaches, volunteers, and supporters who have made this success possible. I look forward to seeing the Bruins continue to grow and inspire future generations. Congratulations again!

tree_branches.name: Keith's Closet
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Keith's Closet
tree_branches.text: Ms KYLIE WILKINSON ( East Hills ) —I would like to recognise the fantastic work of my constituent, Keith Donnelly, whose initiative Keith's Closet has now opened in Shellharbour Hospital and Lismore Mental Health Service. These are the fifth and sixth Keith's Closets to open since the not-for-profit charity began. People living with mental illness in this region now have better access to essential supplies to support their wellbeing, thanks to the expansion of this incredible service. Keith's Closet is a walk-in wardrobe that provides clothing, footwear and toiletries to people navigating severe mental illness or recovery, helping restore dignity and confidence as they focus on treatment. Pioneered by Keith in 2019, when he was working as a Mental Health Clinical Nurse Specialist, Keith's Closet has already made a real difference at Prince of Wales Hospital and other sites across Sydney. Keith, your initiative reflects vision, empathy and a deep commitment to improving mental health care. On behalf of the community, I congratulate you and thank you for your dedication to supporting some of the most vulnerable members of our society. I look forward to the continued expansion of this important initiative.

tree_branches.name: Addison Road Community Centre - Good Food Guide Award
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Addison Road Community Centre - Good Food Guide Award
tree_branches.text: Ms JO HAYLEN ( Sum mer Hill ) —Congratulations to Addison Road Community Centre for winning the prestigious Food for Good award at the Sydney Morning Herald Good Food Guide Awards this week. This honour recognises their unwavering commitment to food justice, sustainability, and community care. Located in Marrickville, Addi Road is a hub of innovation and compassion. From their Food Pantry to their advocacy for equity and inclusion, they continue to uplift the most vulnerable in our community. Under the leadership of CEO Rosanna Barbero, Addi Road has transformed surplus food into dignity and nourishment for thousands, setting a powerful example of grassroots action. However, the real power of Addi Road is the hundreds of volunteers who commit their time and energy to make everything possible. To deliver just the Food Pantry services takes almost 900 volunteers! Winning the Food for Good award is a well-earned recognition of the Centre's impact and the strength of community-led solutions. Congratulations again to Rosanna and the entire Addi Road team‑ you make our community proud.

tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Dakota Heggs
tree_branches.text: Ms SONIA HORNERY ( Wallsend ) —Dakota Heggs from Maryland is only six-years old, and she has shown courage and bravery in a situation that many adults would find distressing. Dakota is a bright young lady who attends Maryland Public School, loves learning, riding her bike and is enjoying her first year of playing netball for a local club. On Thursday, 2 October 2025, Dakota's mum Sharni unfortunately suffered an epileptic seizure. Dakota was asleep in bed and her dad was at work, so there was nobody else in the house to help. Acting quickly, Dakota calmly phoned her grandmother who arranged to get Sharni to hospital. This would have been a confronting experience for most people. Thankfully, Sharni's condition improved. For being a brave little girl, Dakota received a lovely box of chocolates from her appreciative family, and she was proud to note, "I helped Mummy." Dakota, you definitely are a thoughtful, sensible and brave little girl. I hope to hear of more of your wonderful achievements in the future. Well done!

tree_branches.name: Lambton Park War Memorial Swimming Centre
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Lambton Park War Memorial Swimming Centre
tree_branches.text: Ms SONIA HORNERY ( Wallsend ) —Newcastle's first Freshwater Olympic Pool was opened on 26 January 1963 with initial annual operating dates between 1 September and Easter Monday. The occasion was a triumph for the tenacity of a few who worked for the many and a boon for people west of the Gully Line. During WW2, the site now occupied by the pool, was an anti-aircraft gun emplacement with four guns, search-light and a POW camp. Its establishment in western Newcastle had a faltering beginning with some Aldermen opposed during initial discussions in 1958. Funds for the pool were raised by an organising committee, Lake Road and Jesmond Progress Associations, residents of Lambton and other suburbs, raffles, community events, City revenue, the Joint Coal Board, and the Newcastle War Memorial Olympic Pool Committee. Fortnightly levies were also imposed for four years by Leonora Glass Works employees, Wallsend RSL and Lambton Auxiliary. The diving pool was opened on 12 November 1964, operating daily until about 9pm. The pool, now called Lambton Memorial Swimming Centre, is integral to many people's lives, providing enduring memories of growing up. It is important that we remember its roots.

tree_branches.name: Rodney Robb
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Rodney Robb
tree_branches.text: Mr ROY BUTLER ( Barwon ) —Veteran racehorse trainer Rodney Robb has recently retired after 50 years of service to the racing industry in country NSW. Rodney was raised in Nyngan and went on to have a family, all who continue to be connected to the racing industry. Rodney has always maintained his strong connection to country racing rather than taking his horses to the city, partly because of the people out west that made winning more satisfying to the trainer. While Rodney handed over most of his training operations to his son Brett in 2019, he had kept a few horses himself and has not stopped travelling all over the countryside. Clocking up more than two million kilometres, since just 1999, it is clear to see the dedication that Rod has had for his profession, the industry and country racing, especially in the west. I know Rod will be a fixture that is missed across the country tracks of Barwon, but I want to thank him for his commitment to country racing and wish him the very best in his retirement with his family.

tree_branches.name: Mr ROY BUTLER
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Rodney Robb > Mr ROY BUTLER
tree_branches.text: Mr ROY BUTLER ( Barwon ) —2Max FM is a community radio in Narrabri staffed by volunteers. This month 2Max FM celebrates 25 years of broadcasting across the shire. The station has been a trusted source of local news, a platform for local voices, and a lifeline during times of emergency. Operated by dedicated volunteers, the station reflects the spirit of community service and has connected, informed, and entertained the people of Narrabri and surrounds for a quarter of a century. 2MAX FM has provided opportunities for local musicians and presenters, shared stories unique to our region, and built a sense of belonging that strengthens the fabric of our community. I congratulate everyone involved—past and present—in making 2MAX FM such a vital and enduring part of our region. On behalf of the community, I thank them for 25 years of service and look forward to seeing the station continue to grow and thrive into the future.

tree_branches.name: Pearl Blackburn
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Pearl Blackburn
tree_branches.text: Mr ROY BUTLER ( Barwon ) —I'd like to sincerely congratulate Pearl Blackburn, a 17-year-old Cobar local, who has recently been named Orana Young Volunteer of the Year at the recent 2025 Orana Volunteer of the Year Awards held in Dubbo. Pearl volunteers her time with the student council at Cobar High, the Little Athletics Club, Miss Show Girl and Tourism Advisory Committees. While still at school, Pearl also works part-time and is even competing currently overseas in the US at a school cross country event. Young people like Pearl's dedication to her community is admirable and shows maturity beyond her years in juggling so many different things. Seeing this type of commitment to community is a testament to Pearl's character but also highlights what a great generation that are coming up to continue to build a resilient and bright future in bush communities. Well done, Pearl, I look forward to seeing what you continue to accomplish and wish you the very best of luck when you represent the region at the upcoming NSW Volunteer of the Year Awards.

tree_branches.name: David Austin "Tex" Miles
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > David Austin "Tex" Miles
tree_branches.text: Mr ANTHONY ROBERTS ( Lane Cove ) —It is with great joy that I inform the House of the arrival of the first child for the Mayor of Hunters Hill, Zac Miles and his beautiful wife Monica who recently welcomed the birth of David Austin 'Tex' Miles. Tex was born on the 26th of September weighing 2.3kg and measuring at a whopping 52cm. I extend my warmest congratulations to Zac, who is known to many in this House, and of course to Monica in her success of being lighter of a healthy and fair son. I wish them many years of joy ahead together. May this new chapter be filled with love, laughter and lasting memories.

tree_branches.name: Mr ANTHONY ROBERTS
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > David Austin "Tex" Miles > Mr ANTHONY ROBERTS
tree_branches.text: Mr ANTHONY ROBERTS ( Lane Cove ) —Congratulations to the Rotary Club of Lane Cove on hosting such a fantastic fair again this year. It was an outstanding success and truly our biggest and best event yet. The Village Green and the Canopy came alive with families, live music, local stalls and community groups all enjoying a wonderful day together. The Fair is one of the highlights of our local calendar and a great reminder of the community spirit that makes Lane Cove such a special place to live. I want to sincerely thank the Rotary team and all the volunteers who worked tirelessly to make the day run so smoothly. Your efforts bring our community together year after year and continue to make a real difference. Once again this year one of the joys of the day for me was catching up with friends, residents and celebrating another incredible achievement for Rotary and for Lane Cove.

tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Russell Edwards
tree_branches.text: Mrs TINA AYYAD ( Holsworthy ) —I rise to congratulate Mr Russell Edwards, who has been named the 2025 Western Sydney Senior Volunteer of the Year. Russell is a prominent contributor to the community, giving his time as a Justice of the Peace with the NSW Justices Association, a dedicated volunteer with the Fairfield Garden Club, and a self-taught blacksmith at the Fairfield City Museum & Gallery. In the past year alone, he has assisted more than 3,200 people in Fairfield with legal and JP services, providing vital support in one of Australia's most culturally diverse and underserved communities. Russell's commitment to service goes beyond his official duties. Teaching himself blacksmith skills to aid the local museum, and coding to help the museum and JP association, Russell's willingness to step up, learn new skills, and give back reflects his goodwill in supporting the local community.

tree_branches.name: Mrs TINA AYYAD
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Russell Edwards > Mrs TINA AYYAD
tree_branches.text: Mrs TINA AYYAD ( Holsworthy ) —I rise to congratulate Mr Michael Needham, who has been awarded the 2025 Western Sydney Emergency Volunteer of the Year. For more than three decades, Michael has volunteered with St John Ambulance in the Fairfield and Sydney University Divisions, where he has not only delivered vital first aid care to the public but also improved training methods and mentored countless new members. Moreover, he has contributed his expertise to the State Operations Support Group and the Paddington Division, taking on leadership roles in logistics, operations, and clinical education. His dedication is an outstanding example of the impact that emergency volunteers make every day.

tree_branches.name: Ngan Nguyen
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Ngan Nguyen
tree_branches.text: Mrs TINA AYYAD ( Holsworthy ) —I rise to congratulate Ngan Nguyen on being awarded the 2025 Western Sydney Adult Volunteer of the Year. Ngan is a dedicated nursing unit manager and a volunteer with the Community Visitors Scheme at Sydney Multicultural Community Services. In this role, she generously gives her time to regularly visit elderly members of culturally and linguistically diverse communities who are vulnerable to isolation, loneliness, and declining mental health. Through her work, Ngan prioritises building meaningful connections and offering companionship to older people who may have limited family support or face language barriers. I commend her for the positive difference she continues to make in the lives of others.

tree_branches.text: Ms ELENI PETINOS ( Miranda ) —I congratulate Endeavour Sports High School's Student Leadership Team for 2025/2026. I encourage these young leaders to embrace this opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to their school community, to lead with integrity and enthusiasm, and to develop skills that will serve them as the professional and community leaders of tomorrow. I acknowledge the newly appointed Student Leaders: Captains Neve Jenkins and Liam Challenor; Vice Captains Madison Field and Nicholas Mouskos; Senior Prefects Isaac Leonard, Jonathan Mytilinios, and Aysha Youssef; and House Captains Gracie Gardiner, Ryan Lillis, Kenedee Goodwin, Jamie Curran, Shiloh McFarlane-Anning, Cortez Matthews, Sienna Waldau, and Sam Banovic. I also commend the dedicated members of the Student Representative Council — Berry Carr, Chikka Misfud, Taj Morris, Matthew Faulkner, Olivia Hughes, Quinne Hunt, Ethan Moody, Sebastian Thomas, Joel Glasson, Olivia Trieu, Teiana Kapua, Canberra Yamasaki, Zac Brealey, David Begovski, Sasha Croft, Matilda Delfs, Olivia Nolan, and Connor Sharan — for their leadership and school spirit. I wish all student leaders every success as they continue to uphold Endeavour Sports High School's motto of "Valuing individual potential, achieving personal best."

tree_branches.name: North Rocks Shopping Centre
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > North Rocks Shopping Centre
tree_branches.text: Ms MONICA TUDEHOPE ( Epping ) —I ask the Parliament to join with me in congratulating North Rocks Shopping Centre on their 50th anniversary. Established in 1975, North Rocks Shopping Centre has long been a feature of the North Rocks community. When it first opened its doors, it operated as part of the Westfield Group and quickly became a hub for local families, shoppers and small businesses. Over the past five decades, the centre has been a constant presence as the suburb has grown and changed around it. The shopping centre itself serves as a reflection of our changing habits as shoppers. Locals fondly recall when it featured a dine-in Pizza Hut, a Video Ezy store and a Franklins supermarket—icons of earlier eras in Australian retail. Today, it continues to serve the community with a modern offering that includes Coles, Aldi and an indoor swimming centre where many children have learned, and continue to learn, to swim. The 50-year milestone was celebrated with cake, dancing and prizes enjoyed by shoppers and families. Congratulations North Rocks Shopping Centre on reaching this incredible milestone.

tree_branches.name: Ms MONICA TUDEHOPE
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > North Rocks Shopping Centre > Ms MONICA TUDEHOPE
tree_branches.text: Ms MONICA TUDEHOPE ( Epping ) —I ask the Parliament to join with me in recognising the contribution to our community of Joshua James. Joshua James is the manager at Lowes at Carlingford Court. During a recent incident involving a crane at the Carlingford Meriton site, James was working when nearby residents were asked to evacuate their homes and relocate to Carlingford Court. Once an incident was declared, residents were asked to leave immediately, many leaving with out personal items or money, leaving them largely stranded and with no clear timeframe for how long they would be evacuated. The evacuation was sudden and disorienting, and a number of residents were left in distress. Joshua supported residents in this time of distress. He helped residents find accommodation and also brought residents food. Joshua did not act out of obligation or recognition, but out of a simple decency and generosity towards his fellow community members. His conduct reflected the very best of community spirit, and I commend him for his service. I thank Joshua for his service to the residents and to our Carlingford community.

tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > North Rocks Public School Fete
tree_branches.text: Ms MONICA TUDEHOPE ( Epping ) —I ask the Parliament to join me in congratulating the organising committee of the North Rocks Public School Fete. With a circus theme, this fete brought joy to thousands of families from North Rocks and beyond. This event was a reflection of the community spirit that exists in North Rocks, with families coming together to support the school and raise funds for the P&C. Putting on a school fete takes dedication and commitment from volunteers and I would like to thank those parents who gave their time and effort to make this day such a success. In particular, I would like to thank Mrs Cheng Xu for her coordination of the fete. I would also like to give a special mention to the following people for their part in helping make this day a success: Jaythene Hiscock, Thomas McCarthy, Tasha Arhipoff, Lara Scott, Ashley Kelly, Rebecca Read, Paige Montague, Aija Christie, Myra Kim, Brad Wilson, Elie Lim, Megan Bliley, Nicole McGowan, Victoria Targathurai, Gerard Trip, Lisa Msaaey, Daniel Gorrie, Daniella Gorrie, Jenn Mak, Tracey Wilson, Katherine Gallen, Lauren Notley, Robert Santon, Elizabeth Machan, Graham Read and all the parents that were involved across the various teams.

Once an incident was declared, residents were asked to leave immediately, many leaving with out personal items or money, leaving them largely stranded and with no clear timeframe for how long they would be evacuated. The evacuation was sudden and disorienting, and a number of residents were left in distress. Joshua supported residents in this time of distress. He helped residents find accommodation and also brought residents food. Joshua did not act out of obligation or recognition, but out of a simple decency and generosity towards his fellow community members. His conduct reflected the very best of community spirit, and I commend him for his service. I thank Joshua for his service to the residents and to our Carlingford community.

tree_branches.name: Charlie Hindmarsh Travels to Manchester
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Charlie Hindmarsh Travels to Manchester
tree_branches.text: Ms STEPH COOKE ( Cootamundra ) —At just 14 years old, Gundagai's own Charlie Hindmarsh is preparing for the opportunity of a lifetime, heading to Manchester, England, after being selected for an elite squad through the Global Football Network's showcase trials in Sydney. A devoted player since the age of four, Charlie first took to the field with the Panthers Soccer Club in Gundagai. His talent and commitment saw him join the Wagga City Wanderers at 13, and now his years of dedication are being recognised on the international stage. From hundreds of hopefuls, Charlie is one of only 15 players chosen in the under-16s squad to travel to England for a series of trial matches. Joining him for this exciting journey are his proud parents, Belinda and Peter, along with his brothers, Frankie and Henry. Together, they'll not only support Charlie during the trial games but also enjoy a special family holiday to celebrate his 15th birthday. Charlie is to be commended for his devotion to the sport, his dedication to fitness and strength, and his sharp tactical understanding of the game. We wish him every success as he takes this next big step in his football journey.

tree_branches.text: Ms STEPH COOKE ( Cootamundra ) —I wish to recognise the wonderful success of the Illabo Country Music Campout, held recently at the Illabo Showgrounds. Led by local organiser Bill Muller, the event offered a relaxed and inclusive space for artists of all skill levels to perform, connect, and celebrate country music under the stars. Campfires, singalongs, and true community spirit were the hallmarks of the weekend. This grassroots event brought together over 40 country music enthusiasts from across regional NSW including Junee, Temora and Cootamundra. What began as a simple request from past talent quest performers has grown into a cherished annual tradition. While the April Campout remains a staple, this September gathering marked a new chapter and was warmly embraced by all who attended. Importantly, the Campout remains free for all to attend, with only a small fee for those wishing to camp. It is a shining example of how rural communities foster creativity and camaraderie. I commend everyone involved in the Illabo Country Music Campout and look forward to its continued growth in the years to come. Events like this enrich our regions and keep country traditions alive.

tree_branches.name: Through the Lens of Chontelle Perrin
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Through the Lens of Chontelle Perrin
tree_branches.text: Ms STEPH COOKE ( Cootamundra ) —I congratulate Young's own Chontelle Perrin, who has received national acclaim for her outstanding work as a photographer. Chontelle was awarded the top prize at the annual Find A Photographer 'Highlights Photo Awards' for a deeply moving photo of two-year-old Jonah Mills and his parents, taken shortly before Jonah's passing from Stage 4 Neuroblastoma. This prestigious national competition is decided by public vote, reflecting not only the technical quality of Chontelle's work but also the meaningful connections she fosters within the community. Her photograph of Jonah and his family is a poignant tribute that beautifully preserves his memory and highlights the power of photography to capture life's most precious moments. In addition to this heartfelt image, Chontelle also secured second place with a stunning photo of brumbies grazing in the Snowy Mountains, showcasing her versatility and artistic skill. Chontelle's dedication to her craft and her community is inspiring. Her work with the Mills family exemplifies the compassionate role that photographers play in celebrating life and supporting families during difficult times. I congratulate Chontelle Perrin on her well-deserved national recognition and thank her for sharing such meaningful stories through her lens.

tree_branches.name: Saint Vincent de Paul Society Goulburn
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > Saint Vincent de Paul Society Goulburn
tree_branches.text: Mrs WENDY TUCKERMAN ( Goulburn ) — I rise to recognise the Saint Vincent de Paul Society Goulburn. It was back in 1895 following a meeting at St Peter and Paul's Cathedral, which saw the parturition of the Saint Vincent de Paul Society's Goulburn Conference. Recognised as the first non-metropolitan conference to provide unremitting support for those in need. This year celebrating its 130th anniversary on the 27th September with a Mass and morning tea. Irene Picker President, who joined the charity in 2012 has recognised that the foresight shown many, many years earlier has provided support to many people who may have otherwise been left without the assistance needed. The same applies to the eight hundred persons who have accessed assistance more recently. Providing food, clothing, health needs, living expenses, and petrol vouchers. The Christian values encompassed by long term Volunteers like Ross Kirby supports people irrespective of their class creed, or nationality. I sincerely pay my respects to Mrs Picker, and Volunteers who have served the Goulburn community for such an incredibly long period with such care and dignity.

Mrs WENDY TUCKERMAN ( Goulburn ) —I rise to recognise Nerida Duncan. Nerida joined NSW Health in 1972 commencing her General Nurse training at Royal Prince Alfred Hospital, going on to complete her Midwifery training at King George V Hospital between 1975 – 1976. Nerida's career has certainly been comprehensive and varied, working with Sydney Home Nursing Service as a Community Nurse for three years until she commenced her Mothercraft training with the Tresillian Royal Society for Mothers and Infants. Her skills and qualifications also see her as a qualified Nurse Audiometrist and undertaking roles as a Clinical Nurse Specialist and Child and Family Health Nurse going on to join the Goulburn Child Family Health Nurse position based at Goulburn Base Hospital in 2017. After over fifty years of service, she has now decided to retire. I sincerely take this time to acknowledge the phenomenal legacy which Nerida has contributed over such a long period of time and her level of skill and sheer dedication to her roles. I wish you all the very best in the next chapter of your life.

——————————

tree_branches.name: The Hub Crookwell
tree_branches.path: Legislative Assembly (2025-10-14) > Written Community Recognition Statements > The Hub Crookwell
tree_branches.text: Mrs WENDY TUCKERMAN ( Goulburn ) —I rise to recognise The Hub Crookwell. The Crookwell building at 63 Goulburn Street has held a rich history in the township originally opening as a Newsagency by Syd and Dell Davies in 1960, remaining open for sixty-four years before closing and moving into the IGA store. The building has been revitalised, reopening on the 19th September offering five enclosed offices, six open desks, a conference room, a kitchen and everything else needed to operate a business. Enthusiastic owners Floyd and Heather Davies are keen to encourage new small businesses, whilst also being able to support existing home businesses. The energy is high to make The Hub a successful multi-business facility, seeing the Upper Lachlan Gazette already relocating there. The Hub recognises the multi-faceted opportunities to reduce costs, support collaboration and new partnerships. I was proud to attend the opening alongside another 150 individuals and honoured to see Dell Davies officially open The Hub. I congratulate Floyd and Heather on this amazing transformative role of this historic premise and wish them and the broader community every success.
